callout.title: Buy evidence quality before buying more automation
callout.body: The strongest early savings come from reducing invalid claims and repeat handling, not from minimizing every software invoice.
items: Retain the carrier agreement version covering each shipment date; a current contract cannot establish an earlier service guarantee.
Store billed dimensions and corrected dimensions separately, with source evidence; never overwrite the invoice values that explain the dispute.
For cooling-tower sewer adjustments, capture meter serial numbers, installation dates, and municipal acceptance requirements before modeling credits.
Export signed authority and its signature evidence immediately; the recovery file must remain usable after changing signature vendors.

sections.heading: 3. Price actual recovery units and reconcile every operating-cost dollar
paragraphs: The required freight_detention_audit_contingency play starts with authorized UPS, FedEx, and LTL billing feeds, not speculative access to shipper accounts. Obtain signed Letters of Authorization and baseline invoice snapshots before disclosing tariff or refund findings. For an illustrative parcel cohort, 100,000 annual shipments with 1,200 eligible, timely claims averaging $18 produce $21,600 of client recovery. A 40% contingency yields $8,640 of operator revenue, within the play's 35%–50% split range. Neither total shipping spend nor the client's $21,600 refund belongs in operator revenue. If the carrier contract waives service guarantees or suspends a relevant commitment, remove late-delivery claims from the forecast immediately. Pivot toward dimension errors, duplicate charges, LTL classification evidence, and contract-rate benchmarking; these are not dependent on a service-guarantee payout, although their own terms and dispute deadlines still control. For example, 160 substantiated duplicate or rate errors averaging $55 recover $8,800 and earn $3,520 at 40%. Treat that as an alternative cohort, not an automatic addition to the first example. Freight class changes require shipment characteristics and applicable rating rules, not a model's guess. Preserve submission acknowledgments and client credits so the eventual fee invoice can be tied to realized recovery.

Customs work shares ingestion plumbing but requires a separate eligibility and filing workflow. Import CBP Form 7501 entry summaries through the client's authorized broker or ACE export route; do not assume a public read-only API exists for every entry. Match entry lines, duty payments, exported or destroyed merchandise, and claimant rights before describing an amount as eligible for drawback under 19 U.S.C. §1313 and 19 CFR part 190. For an illustrative provision allowing 99% recovery, $20,000 of fully qualifying duties supports $19,800 of potential recovery and a $7,920 fee at 40%, subject to the actual contract and permitted service arrangement. That arithmetic is not a universal eligibility rule. Route filing and customs-business questions to a licensed broker when required, and remove cases lacking export linkage or complete records. Across the volume's 12 mapped plays, reuse evidence storage and collections controls while maintaining distinct eligibility rules. A utility shared-savings example of $2,000 monthly verified savings at 35% earns $700 monthly and $25,200 across 36 months, but only $8,400 during twelve earned months. Never book the full contract duration as first-year operating revenue merely because the agreement was signed. Record baseline changes explicitly when rates, occupancy, or production volumes change.

Reconcile overhead to the canonical scorecard before adding another service. Conservative revenue of $110,000 less $77,000 total costs leaves $33,000 at 30%; Base revenue of $505,000 less $287,850 leaves $217,150 at 43.0%; Scaled revenue of $900,000 less $396,000 leaves $504,000 at 56%. The matrix offers one illustrative cost bridge: annual fixed overhead of $18,000, $60,000, and $114,000, with remaining delivery and other operating costs of $59,000, $227,850, and $282,000. These allocations explain the monthly overhead envelope; they do not replace the canonical totals or imply that all expenses fit inside $1,500–$9,500 monthly. Contractor counts represent available specialist roles, not three or four full-time salaries. Maintain the specified teams of 1 FT + 3 C, 1 FT + 3 C, and 2 FT + 4 C while testing actual capacity separately. Recognize only the operator's earned contractual consideration, assess variable consideration and principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606, and avoid applying the contingency percentage twice. WOTC processing fees should use a documented per-case or other permissible arrangement; employee wages and employer credits are not operator revenue. Count fee collections separately from recognized revenue when testing cash survival.

sections.heading: 4. Launch only after authority, deadlines, restoration, and collections survive testing
paragraphs: Separate commercial expense auditing from regulated representation before the first proposal leaves the business. Treasury Circular 230, 31 CFR §10.27, restricts contingent fees in covered practice and contains specific exceptions; its application must also account for relevant court decisions and the actual service performed. Do not copy a 40% freight recovery clause into federal return preparation or tax-credit representation. Obtain a qualified practitioner's written scope and permissible fee structure, and use Form 2848 or Form 8821 only when its distinct authority fits the task. Property-tax representation requires a state-specific review; Texas Occupations Code chapter 1152 supplies a concrete example of property-tax consultant registration requirements and exceptions. For WOTC, 26 U.S.C. §51(d)(13) generally requires prescreening on or before the offer date and submission to the designated state agency within 28 days after work begins. The statutory termination provision must also be checked for the worker's start date; do not assume a post-2025 extension. Configure ATS reminders around the applicable deadline, retain agency receipts, and exclude ineligible cohorts from sales forecasts. Circular 230 §10.22 reinforces diligence for covered practice, making substantiation a production requirement rather than an optional file-cleanup task.

Run a dry case through the entire production path before accepting a large invoice archive. The case file should contain signed authority, a baseline snapshot, source hashes, extraction results, applicable tariff or contract language, a reviewer decision, and a client-facing calculation. Submit nothing during the rehearsal unless the engagement expressly authorizes that action. Use carrier sandboxes where available, otherwise validate request construction offline and obtain the necessary production permissions. Read-only collection does not authorize filing a claim, changing an account, or communicating with a taxing authority. Test negative cases deliberately: an expired filing window, a waived service guarantee, a previous credit, an employee record missing timely prescreening, and a customs entry without export evidence. Each should produce a specific exception rather than a payable claim. Then disable a contractor account and verify that access disappears from storage, workflow credentials, and shared documents. Restore a deleted test record from backup and confirm its source hash. Record reviewer identity and timestamps without placing sensitive documents in application logs. Launch readiness is a demonstrated chain from lawful access to reproducible fee calculation, not a collection of subscription receipts or a successful login screen.

Finish with a collections rehearsal because technically correct claims can still produce an insolvent business. Agree who receives refunds, what evidence establishes receipt, when fees become due, and how reversals or partial credits are handled. For shared savings, define the baseline, exclusions, measurement period, and dispute process before revealing the opportunity. Simulate a $10,000 client credit with a 35% fee: issue a $3,500 operator invoice only when the contract's earning conditions are satisfied, then test a $2,000 credit reversal and calculate the corresponding $700 fee adjustment where the agreement requires it. Match collected fees to bank activity and keep unresolved differences in an exception queue. The owner reviews reserve coverage weekly; the technical reviewer signs calculation changes; the collections owner confirms receipts without altering claim evidence. These responsibilities can be held by a small team, but conflicting changes should receive independent review. Expand from one repeatable lane only after two closed cases demonstrate source completeness, defensible calculations, timely submission, and collected fees. If municipal issuance stalls, preserve the valid case and shift new production toward shorter-cycle eligible work. Scale the workflow that returns cash, not the dashboard that reports the largest theoretical opportunity.

callout.title: Four pre-flight checks that must produce evidence
callout.body: A reviewer records the result and supporting artifact for each check. A verbal assurance does not satisfy the production checklist.
items: Authority verified: signed client authorization names accounts, records, allowed communications, and separately permitted submissions.
Eligibility verified: contract terms, statutory dates, fee restrictions, and required practitioner credentials match the selected recovery lane.
System verified: least-privilege access, duplicate detection, source hashing, contractor removal, and full case restoration pass recorded tests.
Cash verified: the forecast includes refund delays, committed specialist costs, fee reversals, and at least eight weeks of fixed-cost coverage.

sop_steps.title: Freeze the launch budget
sop_steps.action: Allocate startup cash and segregate at least half as working capital.
sop_steps.detail: Use the endpoint matrix, replace allowances with quotes, and document recurring commitments before spending.

sop_steps.title: Provision the minimum authorized case
sop_steps.action: Configure the twelve layers around one signed engagement and one recovery lane.
sop_steps.detail: Create separate evidence storage, least-privilege credentials, source hashes, and an exportable case record.

sop_steps.title: Rehearse valid and invalid claims
sop_steps.action: Run one supported calculation and the specified negative cases without unauthorized submission.
sop_steps.detail: Retain reviewer decisions, deadline evidence, restoration results, and contractor-access revocation results.

sop_steps.title: Test the fee-to-cash close
sop_steps.action: Simulate client receipt, operator invoicing, fee adjustment, and bank reconciliation.
sop_steps.detail: Update the thirteen-week forecast and release additional production only within demonstrated carrying capacity.

chapters.pull_quote: Buy the evidence pipeline first, protect the collection reserve second by second, and scale only the claims that turn into collected fees.
action_checklist: Segregate $3,300 of a $6,000 launch or $19,000 of a $35,000 launch, and stress-test the reserve against actual refund delays.
Obtain entity banking, covered-activity insurance quotes, contractor terms, and a documented authorized-signer list before receiving client records.
Confirm each named vendor's current tier, regional price, access controls, export path, and cancellation terms before committing recurring spend.
Secure signed Letters of Authorization and unchanged invoice baselines before disclosing tariff findings or requesting production account access.
Run freight_detention_audit_contingency against contract-specific eligibility and maintain dimension, duplicate-charge, classification, and rate-error fallbacks.
Complete the four-step rehearsal, reconcile the canonical scenario cost bridge, and verify collections before expanding into another recovery lane.

chapters.question_prompt: What kills 80% of newcomers in contingent corporate bill-audit & tax-credit recovery, and what forensic metrics detect margin leaks, regulatory landmines, or platform bans before they wipe out capital?
chapters.title: Beginner Traps, Clawbacks & Asymmetric Failure Modes
chapters.subtitle: FedEx and UPS Waivers, Utility Refund Aging, Property-Appeal Deadlines, WOTC Evidence, and Circular 230 Fee Boundaries
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #38, Rank #06 of 42, scores 94/100 because small teams can monetize documented recoveries without owning the underlying expense base. Its twelve mapped plays nevertheless share lethal weaknesses: waived carrier remedies, unstable savings baselines, unauthorized filings, expired deadlines, defective employee certifications, and revenue booked before entitlement exists. This chapter turns those weaknesses into measurable stop rules across parcel, utility, waste, telecom, property-tax, and credit work. Formula v2.0 annual owner profit remains $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled. Those outcomes require earned operator fees, not client refund totals masquerading as revenue. Build evidence-linked billing, licensed local coverage, reversal reserves, and credential isolation before multiplying claim volume.

sections.heading: 1. Kill False Entitlement Before Automating Twelve Recovery Plays
paragraphs: The question's 80% figure is a framing device, not an observed failure rate; no cohort evidence supports that percentage here. The operational problem is concrete: newcomers automate candidate discovery before proving entitlement. Organize the twelve mapped plays as parcel service refunds, parcel duplicate charges, parcel accessorial corrections, utility tariff corrections, utility meter corrections, cooling-tower sewer exclusions, waste invoice corrections, telecom inventory cleanup, telecom contract-rate corrections, property-tax appeals, WOTC processing, and specialty tax-credit recovery. These are operational mappings, not twelve independently scored businesses. For each, preserve the signed Letter of Authorization, governing contract version, original invoice, calculation, filing deadline, and payment evidence. A FedEx or UPS service delay can produce zero collectible recovery when the applicable service guarantee is suspended, contractually waived, or subject to an exclusion. Suppose software flags 1,000 shipments with $20 potential refunds: $20,000 is candidate exposure, not operator revenue. If only 400 qualify and settle, a 35% earned share produces $2,800 before delivery costs. Submitting all 1,000 does not improve that arithmetic; it adds rejection handling and account risk. Freeze the affected service lane when waiver coverage cannot be established, then inspect the actual contract and current carrier terms before resuming.

Duplicate billing and accessorial correction are different defects from late delivery, so route them through their applicable dispute processes rather than assuming every claim shares a guarantee deadline. Reconcile tracking identifier, invoice number, charge code, account, and adjustment identifier before submission. A $15 credit already issued cannot support another $5.25 fee at a 35% split. Set the duplicate-submission target to zero, and quarantine a batch when its internal duplicate rate exceeds 0.5%; this is an illustrative operating threshold, not a carrier rule. For utility tariff and meter work, compare rate class, demand interval, meter multiplier, and occupancy against the governing tariff. Cooling-tower sewer exclusions require the local utility's accepted measurement and application process; an equipment photograph alone does not establish deductible discharge volume. A verified $12,000 utility refund at 30% supports $3,600 of operator fees, whereas an engineering estimate supports only a prospect record. Waste audits must reconcile container count, pickup frequency, contamination charges, and contract escalators. Stop a projected $500 monthly saving when a replacement contract adds $600 in minimum charges. The fallback is a narrower invoice correction, not a fabricated service dispute or pressure campaign against a vendor.

Telecom inventory cleanup fails when an apparently idle circuit carries alarm traffic, emergency routing, or backup connectivity. Require a customer-owned dependency map and written disconnect authority before issuing a termination request. Telecom contract-rate corrections need service-order dates, promotional expirations, minimum commitments, and early termination charges in the same calculation. Ten unused lines costing $80 monthly suggest $800 of gross savings; $300 of unavoidable replacement service reduces the defensible baseline to $500. A 40% share then produces $200 monthly, not $320, and a 36-month arrangement yields $7,200 only if all required months actually qualify. Separate historical refund shares from prospective savings splits so the same correction does not generate two fees. Establish a baseline hierarchy using signed contracts, invoice snapshots, measured usage, and documented adjustments for seasonality or site closures. Keep client-requested scope changes outside the original savings denominator. Pause billing whenever an unresolved baseline variance exceeds 5% of the proposed fee; release the invoice only after an identified reviewer resolves the difference. The reliable fallback is verified realized savings billed monthly, with a clearly defined termination reconciliation, rather than accelerating three years of hypothetical benefit into today's earnings.

sections.heading: 2. Separate Lawful Filing Authority From Attractive Recovery Math
paragraphs: The play property_tax_assessment_appeal_contingency begins when the county releases annual valuation notices, not when a generic national deadline appears on a calendar. Ingest the assessor roll, retain its publication date and parcel identifiers, and run an automated valuation model that flags assessments above defensible comparable-neighbor equity ratios. Screen sales comparables, property condition, use, exemptions, and local assessment rules before treating an AVM signal as an appeal. A $1,000,000 assessment reduced to $900,000 at an illustrative 2% effective tax rate produces $2,000 of first-year tax reduction; a 40% contingency produces $800, not $40,000. The stated 30–50% range applies to verified tax reduction, never the assessed-value reduction. Local rules may use different taxable-value mechanics, so reconcile the actual corrected bill. Texas Tax Code §41.44 generally ties protest timing to May 15 or thirty days after delivery of the notice, whichever is later, with additional statutory exceptions. Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1152 regulates property-tax consultants subject to its scope and exemptions. Partner with qualified local consultants or attorneys of record where required, and automate pre-deadline batch electronic filing only after representation authority and portal acceptance are documented.

WOTC processing fails asymmetrically because an inexpensive missing document can destroy the entire expected credit. Under 26 U.S.C. §51, the employer must satisfy the applicable targeted-group, certification, wage, and service requirements. Form 8850 prescreening generally must be completed on or before the employment offer, and the certification request generally must reach the designated local agency within twenty-eight days after work begins. Preserve the offer date, signature events, start date, transmission receipt, agency determination, qualifying hours, and wages. Do not backdate forms or infer an employee's eligibility from neighborhood demographics. For many eligible groups, $6,000 of qualified first-year wages at 40% yields a maximum $2,400 credit after the relevant 400-hour threshold; other groups and circumstances differ. A $150 processing fee remains $150 of operator revenue, not $2,400. Section 51(c)(4) contains a December 31, 2025 commencement cutoff; verify any enacted extension before representing later starts as eligible. Agency acceptance of paperwork alone does not establish a statutory extension. Escalate cases at day twenty-one, and stop representing a missed deadline as recoverable unless a specific applicable relief provision or agency procedure actually supports that treatment.

Specialty tax-credit recovery adds a different trap: copying the expense audit contingency agreement into federal return preparation. Treasury Circular 230 §10.27 restricts contingent fees in covered federal tax matters and specifies exceptions; judicial decisions also limit aspects of its reach. Have the responsible tax professional determine the permitted engagement structure for the actual service, rather than assuming every amended return qualifies for a refund exception. Separate fixed processing charges, permitted recovery compensation, return preparation, and representation in the scope and ledger. A proposed $50,000 credit with a 20% recovery share suggests $10,000 only if the fee arrangement is permissible and the compensation is earned. It does not justify filing an unsupported position. Preserve wage allocations, project records, eligibility analyses, and reconciliation against other incentives where double use is restricted. Circular 230 §10.22 requires diligence within its scope; 26 U.S.C. §6694 addresses specified preparer understatement conduct. Route uncertain positions to the responsible practitioner and suspend unsupported submissions. The fallback is a documented eligibility study or properly priced processing engagement, not rebranding return preparation as consulting while leaving the same prohibited fee economics and unsupported claims intact.

sections.heading: 3. Detect Clawbacks, Baseline Drift, and Cash Conversion Failure
paragraphs: Formula v2.0 counts earned contingency refund shares, earned shared-savings splits, and WOTC processing fees as operator revenue. It excludes the client's underlying freight, utility, property-tax, and wage base, and it excludes client recoveries belonging to the client. The Conservative case is $110,000 revenue less $77,000 costs, leaving $33,000 at 30%. Base is $505,000 less $287,850, leaving $217,150 at 43.0%. Scaled is $900,000 less $396,000, leaving $504,000 at 56%. Teams remain 1 FT plus 3 C, 1 FT plus 3 C, and 2 FT plus 4 C, respectively. These are the canonical annual cases, not forecasts rebuilt from example claims. Where the operator acts as agent, apply the ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to the promised service and present the retained fee appropriately; routing a client's refund through an operator bank account does not create gross operator revenue. Recognition also depends on performance obligations and constrained variable consideration, not merely an internal discovery status. Keep candidate recovery, submitted recovery, approved adjustment, client receipt, earned fee, invoice, and operator collection as separate fields. Their differences explain why a persuasive pipeline can coexist with an empty payroll account.

Clawbacks are usually contractual and evidentiary before they become accounting problems. A carrier can reverse an erroneous credit; a utility can correct a provisional adjustment; a tax authority can disallow a credit; and a client can dispute whether an expense reduction belongs to the agreed baseline. Define whether each event reduces an unpaid invoice, requires repayment, offsets future fees, or triggers an indemnity review. For an illustrative $100,000 collected recovery at a 35% split, the operator initially earns $35,000 only under the applicable recognition and contract conditions. If $20,000 of the underlying recovery is later reversed and the agreement passes that reversal through proportionally, operator exposure is $7,000. Do not assume exposure stops there if the contract shifts penalties, interest, or defense costs. Model those obligations separately and negotiate clear allocation before signing. A provisional reserve of 10% of exposed fees would hold $3,500 and would not cover that $7,000 event. Calibrate reserves from actual claim cohorts, reversal severity, and open disputes rather than a comforting round percentage. Segregate client funds from operating cash and prefer direct client receipt where the engagement permits it, reducing both custody complexity and false liquidity.

Monitor cash conversion by recovery lane because municipal refunds and parcel credits rarely share the same issuance cycle. Define recovery aging from accepted submission to client receipt, invoice aging from fee invoice to payment, and reversal rate as reversed earned fees divided by the corresponding cohort's earned fees. Illustrative intervention thresholds are invoice aging above sixty days, utility issuance beyond the documented expected date by thirty days, fee reversals above 3% over a rolling ninety-day cohort, and more than 20% of receivables concentrated in one client. These are management choices, not statutory limits. Stop expanding the affected lane when two thresholds breach together; continue valid deadline-sensitive work while fixing collection terms and evidence defects. Track handling cost per accepted claim: a $12 fee requiring twenty minutes at $45 hourly costs $15 in direct labor before software or overhead, creating a negative $3 contribution. Batch only cases sharing the same evidence standard and use minimum viable recovery thresholds defined in the engagement. The stated $1,500–$9,500 monthly operating range is not the complete annual cost stack; contractor, staffing, and delivery costs must still reconcile to each canonical scenario's total costs.

sections.heading: 4. Install Circuit-Breakers Before Credentials, Filings, or Clients Fail
paragraphs: The fastest route to a platform ban is treating access as permission to ignore the platform's operating rules. Use authorized FedEx and UPS integrations only for the endpoints, accounts, and purposes actually enabled; do not assume every refund action has a public API. Where a permitted electronic claim interface is unavailable, use the approved portal or documented service channel. Shared client passwords, fabricated tracking records, repeated duplicate claims, account rotation after suspension, and bypassing rate limits convert a recoverable workflow defect into a trust failure. Store delegated credentials in a managed secret store, separate clients by access scope, and record which identity submitted each transaction. Treat any confirmed cross-client access as an immediate stop condition. Treat repeated authorization errors as a credential incident, not an invitation to retry with broader access. For rate-limit responses, honor the published retry policy and reduce concurrency; do not distribute the same prohibited workload across replacement identities. Keep an emergency disable switch per carrier, client, and action type so one broken submission path does not halt safe invoice ingestion. Preserve the platform notice and request reinstatement through its stated process rather than creating an undisclosed replacement account.

Tax and employee records require tighter separation than ordinary invoice totals. WOTC packets can contain sensitive identifiers and eligibility information that should never appear in shared claim queues or general sales notes. Restrict access by assigned task, encrypt stored documents, and log exports. When acting as a tax return preparer within the relevant rules, assess 26 U.S.C. §7216 and 26 CFR §301.7216-3 before using or disclosing return information outside permitted purposes. An expense-audit Letter of Authorization is not automatically a valid tax-information disclosure consent. Minimize information copied into OCR prompts, support tickets, and contractor worksheets; approved service providers still require a purpose and access boundary. For utility meter OCR, compare extracted multipliers and billing periods with source images, and route material mismatches to human review. A single misplaced decimal can inflate a claimed recovery tenfold. Use amount and date reconciliation rather than trusting the OCR engine's confidence score alone. Quarantine documents with missing account identifiers or inconsistent totals before any external filing. Preserve records under the engagement's applicable retention schedule and suspend routine deletion when an audit, dispute, or preservation obligation requires the evidence to remain available.

Run a weekly exception meeting around recoverability, not the number of claims generated. Review the ten largest proposed fees, every missed deadline, every reversal, unresolved authorization failures, and any client whose direct handling costs exceed earned fees. Assign an owner and next action to each exception; otherwise the dashboard merely decorates the failure. Before scaling a lane, replay a sample from original invoice through authorized submission, client receipt, earned fee, and collection. An illustrative sampling rule is twenty cases per active lane each month, expanded to the entire affected batch when a material eligibility defect appears. A sample is process surveillance, not proof that every unsampled claim is valid. For property-tax batches, preserve portal acknowledgments per parcel; a successful upload does not establish acceptance of every protest. For thirty-six-month savings agreements, recheck usage and contract changes at each billing cycle. For WOTC, reconcile certifications with payroll hours and qualified wages before passing amounts to the responsible preparer. The circuit-breaker succeeds when it contains the defective lane without abandoning valid client obligations. Resume only after the root cause is corrected, affected cases are reconciled, and a named reviewer documents the successful replay.

sop_steps.title: Quarantine the smallest affected operating lane
sop_steps.action: Disable the implicated client, service, credential, or submission action.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve safe ingestion and valid deadline-sensitive work; record the incident time, responsible operator, and affected claim identifiers.

sop_steps.title: Reconstruct authority and entitlement
sop_steps.action: Replay the disputed cases from original evidence and governing rules.
sop_steps.detail: Check signed authorization, contract versions, statutory timing, duplicate adjustments, professional scope, and parcel-level or claim-level receipts.

sop_steps.title: Reconcile fee and client exposure
sop_steps.action: Separate client recovery reversals from operator fees and additional obligations.
sop_steps.detail: Calculate credits, repayments, reserve changes, handling costs, and any contractually allocated penalties or defense costs without treating client funds as operating cash.

sop_steps.title: Verify the fix before restoring submissions
sop_steps.action: Require a named reviewer to approve an evidence-complete replay.
sop_steps.detail: Restore only the corrected scope, monitor the next batch, and document remaining disputes, approaching deadlines, and client communications.

chapters.pull_quote: A recovery business scales on defensible entitlement and collected fees, not on the size of the bills it touches.
action_checklist: Build a twelve-lane entitlement register linking each recovery type to its contract, statute, authorization, filing route, and fee trigger.
Reconcile the Conservative, Base, and Scaled ledgers to $33,000, $217,150, and $504,000 annual owner profit without counting client recoveries as revenue.
Install duplicate detection, carrier waiver checks, parcel-level filing receipts, and WOTC date controls before increasing automated submissions.
Have the responsible practitioner review federal tax compensation structures and verify local property-tax representation credentials.
Measure claim handling contribution, invoice aging, cohort fee reversals, and client concentration using documented intervention thresholds.
Test client-scoped credential isolation and rehearse a submission shutdown that preserves evidence and valid deadline-sensitive obligations.

chapters.question_prompt: Where do high-margin deals, clients, or undervalued assets hide in contingent corporate bill-audit & tax-credit recovery, and what repeatable outbound/inbound sourcing system lands the first 3-to-10 wins (1–4 months)?
chapters.title: Sourcing, Demand Mining & Landing Your First Deals
chapters.subtitle: Mine Carrier Contracts, Utility Tariffs, Assessment Rolls and Hiring Signals; Convert Authorized Evidence into Collectible Recovery Fees
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #38, ranked #06 of 42 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, wins through evidence access rather than spectacular refund promises. This chapter organizes 12 mapped plays into a practical sourcing system spanning parcel, utility, waste, telecom, assessment and employer-credit opportunities. Start with observable billing complexity, qualify contractual rights, secure signed authorization, then price an attributable result. The canonical annual owner profits are $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base and $504,000 Scaled; client bills and tax credits never become operator revenue. Build toward three to ten signed mandates within one to four months, while tracking cash recoveries separately. Use narrow account lists, professional referrals and documented baseline snapshots to prevent weak claims, prohibited tax-fee arrangements and long collection cycles from consuming the small team's capacity.

key_metrics.label: Conservative
key_metrics.context: Annual operator revenue from earned recovery shares, shared savings and processing fees
key_metrics.note: 30% net margin; $33,000 annual owner net profit; 1 FT + 3 C

key_metrics.label: Base
key_metrics.context: Annual operator revenue excluding underlying client bills, credits and principal
key_metrics.note: 43.0% net margin; $217,150 annual owner net profit; 1 FT + 3 C

key_metrics.label: Scaled
key_metrics.context: Annual operator revenue including earned portions of contracted shared savings
key_metrics.note: 56% net margin; $504,000 annual owner net profit; 2 FT + 4 C

sections.heading: 1. Mine twelve sourcing lanes for observable, collectible billing friction
paragraphs: Start with organizations whose operational complexity creates repeatable invoice errors, not companies merely described as spending heavily. Build the first list around regional distributors, multi-location retailers, hotels, light manufacturers and hourly-workforce employers. Use company location pages, municipal permit portals, assessor rolls, public procurement awards and employer career pages to identify a dated change: an acquisition, warehouse opening, cooling-tower installation, reassessment or hiring surge. Record the source URL, observation date, affected operating entity and hypothesis in HubSpot or a structured spreadsheet. A permit establishes equipment or construction activity; it does not establish overbilling. A job advertisement establishes recruiting intent; it does not establish worker eligibility for a credit. Pair each signal with a document request that could disprove the hypothesis quickly. For example, a new distribution center suggests a parcel-contract review, but the decisive evidence is the executed carrier agreement and recent invoice detail. Avoid collecting shipment addresses or applicant records during prospecting. Ask for aggregate activity first, then move sensitive evidence into a client-controlled workspace after authorization. Rank a source higher when it identifies both a budget owner and a claim deadline, because access and timing determine whether theoretical savings become a payable engagement.

Use twelve operational plays as the chapter's sourcing map, without pretending that every lane has identical economics. The first seven are parcel service-guarantee recovery, parcel duplicate-billing correction, parcel address-and-dimension adjustment review, electric tariff classification, demand-ratchet correction, cooling-tower sewer deduction and water-meter multiplier correction. These are distinct evidence patterns, even when one client supports several. A distributor with $300,000 of annual parcel charges might reveal $6,000 of recoverable errors in an illustrative authorized review; a 35% fee produces $2,100 of operator revenue, not $300,000. If a service-guarantee waiver blocks the first lane, investigate separately documented duplicate charges rather than relabeling late deliveries. For a cooling-tower prospect, 1,000 eligible avoided sewer units at a hypothetical $6 tariff create $6,000 of client benefit and $2,100 at the same fee. Actual units, meter certification and effective dates must come from the applicable utility rule. If the municipality requires a dedicated meter, sell a prospective measurement project rather than claim unsupported historical deductions. Each lane needs a named evidence owner, a governing contract or tariff, a filing route and a fallback that preserves a useful client relationship without manufacturing recoveries.

The remaining five plays are waste-service reconciliation, telecom inventory cleanup, property-assessment appeals, cross-site shared-savings verification and the employer-credit engine identified in the next section. Waste opportunities appear after occupancy changes, dumpster replacements or acquisitions; telecom opportunities appear when offices close but circuits remain billed. Property opportunities begin with assessor records and appeal calendars, not an assumption that a recent purchase automatically proves excessive value. Cross-site verification compares equivalent facilities after normalizing occupancy, weather, throughput and rate changes. An illustrative waste correction of $800 monthly supports $9,600 of annual client savings; a 30% share yields $2,880 only as qualifying savings are earned. Four disconnected telecom circuits costing $250 monthly create $1,000 monthly savings and a $300 monthly fee at 30%. A property appeal yielding an actual $20,000 tax reduction produces $5,000 at a permissible 25% fee, subject to local licensing and contract terms. If an appeal deadline has passed, calendar the next assessment cycle rather than promise retroactive relief. For shared savings of $1,000 monthly, a 30% split over 36 months has a $10,800 nominal contract value, but only $3,600 belongs to the first full year of earned fees. These examples are qualification arithmetic, not additional annual scorecard scenarios.

callout.title: Find the owner of the evidence before pitching the owner of the budget
callout.body: The strongest prospect combines a timely trigger, accessible records and a remedy that the counterparty actually honors.
items: Ask parcel prospects for the guarantee-waiver page before pricing the audit; a large shipment count cannot cure an excluded contractual remedy.
Read municipal sewer-deduction instructions before contacting hotels; a required certified submeter changes the pitch from historical recovery to prospective measurement.
Match property appeal calendars to the assessor's notice date, then verify who may represent the owner before scheduling an acquisition campaign.
Ask referral accountants which clients already have active recovery vendors; a clean exclusion list prevents duplicate claims and fee disputes.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify authority, fee legality and expected contribution before accepting a mandate
paragraphs: Score every prospect on six dimensions totaling 100 points: evidence accessibility 25, enforceable recovery basis 20, expected operator contribution 20, decision-maker access 15, filing runway 10 and collection speed 10. These weights are an operating heuristic, not historical performance data. Require at least 75 points and no fatal defect before assigning a specialist. Fatal defects include missing authorization, an expired filing window without an available remedy, prohibited representation or an unusable fee arrangement. Estimate contribution from collectible operator fees, not client expenditure. A prospect with a plausible $10,000 refund and a 35% fee starts at $3,500 revenue. Subtract an illustrative $700 specialist charge and $300 direct processing cost to obtain $2,500 contribution before shared overhead. If recovery probability is provisionally 50%, the probability-weighted fee is $1,750; subtracting $1,000 costs committed regardless of outcome leaves $750. If costs depend on success, model that dependency separately instead of applying one haircut to everything. Record which inputs are client-confirmed and which remain assumptions. Set an initial analyst-hour ceiling and a stop condition. A smaller account with complete records and a short payment cycle can outrank a prestigious prospect whose legal entity, vendor contract and authorized signer remain unresolved.

Treat wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine as a specialized twelfth play, not a blanket permission to charge a percentage of tax savings. Its full scope is Automated Form 8850 WOTC (Work Opportunity Tax Credit) & Section 41 R&D Contingency Engine — TRACK_1. Begin with employer-authorized screening, applicable hiring dates and state workforce agency procedures. Section 51(c)(4) establishes a statutory cutoff for workers beginning employment after December 31, 2025; verify any enacted extension before marketing eligibility for later hires. The Section 51(d)(13) prescreening route generally requires the prescreening notice by the employment-offer date and submission within 28 days after work begins. Do not mistake a hiring feed for permission to collect applicant eligibility information. For an illustrative eligible worker meeting the 400-hour threshold, $6,000 of qualified first-year wages at 40% produces a $2,400 credit, subject to the worker category and wage limits. Twenty such certified workers produce $48,000 of client credits, not operator revenue. A permissible $150 fixed processing fee per completed eligible case produces $3,000. If authorization, timing or substantiation fails, exclude the claim and offer fixed-fee payroll documentation under independent tax review rather than backdating forms or promising a credit.

Separate Section 41 research work from WOTC screening, even when the same employer buys both services. Engineering job postings, prototype facilities and new manufacturing processes justify a discovery call, but they do not establish qualified research. Request project-level evidence addressing technological uncertainty, a permitted purpose and a process of experimentation, with expenses tied to actual activities. An illustrative alternative simplified credit calculation with $100,000 current qualified research expenses and a $120,000 three-year average gives a $60,000 threshold; 14% of the $40,000 excess is $5,600 before applicable elections and adjustments. This is a calculation example, not a determination of eligibility. Review funded-research exclusions, controlled-group rules, wage coordination and Section 280C treatment separately. Treasury Circular 230, 31 CFR 10.27, restricts contingent fees in covered matters and contains specific exceptions; judicial decisions also affect its reach. Have the responsible practitioner resolve the engagement's actual fee treatment before selling an outcome-linked arrangement. A $2,000 fixed documentation engagement is operator revenue only as the contracted service is earned, not a share of $100,000 research spending. Where evidence is weak, stop the credit work and preserve only supportable documentation services, with an independent tax professional controlling the return position.

callout.title: Four checks before evidence leaves the client's control
callout.body: A high qualification score cannot substitute for authority, a timely remedy or a workable engagement contract.
items: Obtain a signed engagement and Letter of Authorization naming entities, accounts, permitted actions, representatives and an expiration or revocation mechanism.
Preserve dated baseline invoices and identify prior credits, incumbent auditors, excluded sites and the exact recovery window before presenting detailed findings.
Verify carrier terms, utility procedures, local property-tax representation requirements and the responsible practitioner's tax-fee determination for the actual service.
Confirm lawful hiring dates, required WOTC timing, secure applicant-data handling and independent substantiation before accepting any employer-credit claim.

sections.heading: 3. Run a permission-conscious outreach cadence with explicit funnel denominators
paragraphs: Build an initial 400-account research universe, then remove accounts lacking a relevant trigger, reachable role or viable remedy. An illustrative campaign retains 160 evidence-qualified contacts, generates 32 substantive replies, books 16 discovery calls, qualifies ten opportunities and signs six mandates. That is a 40% research-to-contact yield, 20% contact-to-reply rate, 50% reply-to-call rate, 62.5% call-to-qualified rate and 60% qualified-to-signed rate. These are planning assumptions, not market benchmarks established by a dataset. The overall signed rate is 1.5% of raw accounts and 3.75% of contacted accounts. Track unique accounts separately from individual recipients so multiple contacts cannot inflate conversion. If only eight replies arrive, inspect targeting and message evidence before increasing volume. If calls occur but mandates stall, inspect authority, data burden, incumbent exclusions and fee clarity. Use three to ten signed engagements as the first one-to-four-month objective; municipal refunds, property appeals and tax outcomes may settle substantially later. Add a separate realized-value stage for credits posted, refunds received or accepted processing services completed. In the example, three of six mandates might reach that stage within the observation window, but the other three remain open inventory rather than hidden failures or booked revenue.

Use a bounded, multichannel sequence built around one verifiable trigger. On day one, send a short business email identifying the observed event, the narrow audit category and the two documents needed to decide whether a review is worthwhile. On day three, make a manual call to the published business number and ask who owns that invoice category. On day six, send a plain-language evidence checklist without asking for account passwords or applicant records. On day ten, offer a 15-minute triage call with the controller and operating owner. On day fifteen, close the sequence and state that further contact will stop unless they request follow-up. Check suppression lists before every touch. Commercial email must satisfy applicable CAN-SPAM requirements, including accurate routing information, nondeceptive subject lines, a valid postal address and a working opt-out honored within ten business days. Do not treat a business label as exemption from every telephone rule; calling technology, number type, message content and state requirements matter. Avoid automated dialing or prerecorded messages unless the applicable requirements have been established. LinkedIn outreach should be manual and relevant, not a workaround for an email opt-out. Log each contact's source, channel, outcome and next permitted action.

Make inbound and partner channels answer the same narrow question as outbound: which records prove whether a recoverable discrepancy exists? Publish a carrier-waiver checklist, a cooling-tower deduction evidence guide and a property-notice deadline worksheet, each directing readers to a scoped intake form. Explain the actual state or utility jurisdiction covered rather than collecting broad search traffic with unsupported nationwide claims. Ask CPAs, payroll implementers, commercial property managers and fractional controllers for introductions to a specific account pattern. Obtain client permission before exchanging sensitive details, and review professional restrictions before paying referral compensation. A useful opening is, 'Your new warehouse may have changed account-level parcel terms; we review the waiver and two invoices before proposing a claim.' When the prospect says their accountant already handles this, offer to work within the accountant's defined scope and exclude overlapping claims. When they fear vendor retaliation, explain the ordinary billing-dispute route and decline any promise about the vendor's future behavior. When they demand a free list of recoveries, offer a redacted sample deliverable and a bounded diagnostic. Do not disclose account-specific tariff findings before the signed authorization and baseline snapshots are secured. Every objection should end with a concrete next step or a clean disqualification.

sections.heading: 4. Turn first mandates into verified benefits, collected fees and repeatable referrals
paragraphs: Structure the first mandate around a bounded account set and a measurable remedy. The engagement should identify covered entities, invoice periods, excluded claims, fee percentages, settlement authority, evidence retention, payment timing and treatment of preexisting credits. Obtain a separate or clearly delineated Letter of Authorization that the carrier, utility or other counterparty will accept. Request read-only exports or delegated access where supported; never ask a prospect to email shared administrator credentials. Preserve original invoice files, extraction versions and reconciliation outputs so a later reviewer can reproduce the finding. Carrier APIs, EDI feeds and OCR improve throughput only when the client has authorized their use and vendor terms permit the integration. Do not assume every FedEx or UPS account has the same claims API or guarantee coverage. For each proposed correction, link the contractual or tariff provision to the invoice line, calculation and submission deadline. Have the client approve any account changes or settlements outside delegated authority. Report a submitted claim as submitted, an accepted adjustment as accepted and a received refund as received. This discipline prevents an attractive dashboard from becoming an unpaid-fee dispute when the vendor reverses a provisional credit or the client identifies an earlier adjustment.

Manage the first four months as a queue with explicit work limits. During weeks one and two, select two adjacent invoice lanes, establish specialist coverage and build the first 100-account batch. During weeks three and four, complete the initial outreach cycle, conduct triage calls and close the first narrow mandates where evidence is ready. During months two and three, submit timely claims, issue evidence-backed status updates and expand only into accounts sharing the same document pattern. During month four, seek introductions from clients with verified benefits and review whether collection delays justify changing the target segment. One founder can own sourcing, scope and client communication while three contractors provide parcel, utility and tax-specialist capacity; contractor headcount does not imply three full-time salaries. The canonical startup capital range is $6,000–$35,000 and monthly operating range is $1,500–$9,500, but neither replaces a fully loaded annual cost budget. Reserve cash for contractor invoices that precede recovery receipts. Municipal queues and property calendars can exceed the initial selling window, so balance them with shorter-cycle invoice corrections. If evidence retrieval repeatedly consumes more than the agreed diagnostic ceiling, pause the account and request a specific missing artifact instead of subsidizing an open-ended investigation.

Reconcile performance to the canonical Formula v2.0 cases without converting client savings into operator sales. Conservative operator revenue is $110,000, with $77,000 total costs and $33,000 owner net profit at 30%, supported by 1 FT + 3 C. Base revenue is $505,000, with $287,850 costs and $217,150 profit at 43.0%, also supported by 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled revenue is $900,000, with $396,000 costs and $504,000 profit at 56%, supported by 2 FT + 4 C. These are annual scorecard cases, not a forecast for the first six mandates. Earned contingency shares, earned portions of 36-month savings arrangements and completed processing services provide the revenue basis. Do not add the underlying refund, utility expenditure, employer credit or full nominal savings contract to revenue. Apply the actual contract and applicable revenue-recognition treatment, including variable consideration and principal-versus-agent presentation, rather than treating gross cash passing through an account as sales. Keep expected fees, recognized revenue, receivables and collected cash in separate columns. Ask for referrals after the client confirms the benefit and understands the fee calculation. The repeatable asset is a documented remedy attached to a reliable evidence workflow, not a growing inventory of optimistic claims.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #38, Contingent Corporate Bill-Audit & Tax-Credit Recovery, holds Rank #06 of 42 with a Money-to-Manpower Score of 94/100. This chapter turns 12 mapped plays into one controlled production line: authorize access, freeze evidence, verify eligibility, submit once, prove client benefit, earn the fee, and reconcile operator cash. Six copy-pasteable engineering modules define a transactional SQLite subledger without treating client recoveries as operator revenue. The worked cohort earns $126,250 over 90 days, exactly one quarter of the $505,000 Base revenue case, while exposing collection lag and $10,000 closing receivables. Annual owner profit remains $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled; tax-service restrictions determine compensation structure before any engagement starts.

sections.heading: 1. Convert twelve recovery plays into authorized, evidence-complete work packets
paragraphs: Start with a signed engagement, a narrowly scoped Letter of Authorization, and a baseline invoice snapshot before revealing recoverable findings. Record the legal customer, billing account, service location, covered period, permitted access method, submission deadline, fee trigger, and refund destination. The customer receives the supplier refund directly; the operator separately invoices an earned service fee. Obtain FedEx or UPS contract schedules before testing service guarantees because a negotiated waiver can erase an apparently attractive late-delivery claim. Use authorized EDI exports or documented carrier interfaces where access exists, rather than assuming every developer account includes refund submission. For utilities, preserve tariff sheets, meter identifiers, interval histories, sewer factors, and municipal credit policies. Freeze original files with SHA-256 digests; retain OCR output as a derivative, never as the sole evidence. Intake scores authorization and baseline integrity at 25 points each, deadline and contract eligibility at 20 each, and an identified payer at ten. A score below 100 can prioritize remediation but cannot authorize submission. This deliberately separates sales enthusiasm from production readiness and makes rejected work visible before contractors spend scarce review hours.

Map the shelf into twelve operational lanes, not twelve different businesses. Parcel service refunds, duplicate parcel charges, and dimensional corrections share invoice ingestion but require different evidence. Utility tariff changes, cooling-tower sewer abatements, utility tax exemptions, waste true-ups, and telecom disconnects share site ownership records but not eligibility rules. Property assessment appeals need jurisdiction-specific authority and qualified representation. WOTC processing, specialty-credit documentation, and Section 179D allocation support belong in separate tax-service workspaces with distinct fee terms. The matrix supplies illustrative unit economics for all twelve; only the refund lanes enter the worked cohort. A $20,000 verified supplier recovery at 25% produces $5,000 of operator revenue, not $20,000. A $1,000 monthly verified saving at a 30% split produces $300 per qualifying month, not an immediate $10,800 receivable merely because the contract runs 36 months. Specify the counterfactual baseline, volume adjustments, termination rights, and disputed-month treatment before starting. Keep proposed benefits, earned fees, invoiced balances, and bank receipts in separate fields so commercial forecasts cannot quietly become accounting entries during a busy weekly close.

Treat section_179d_municipal_deduction_allocation_arbitrage as TRACK_1 coordination of an eligible owner, qualifying designer, and independent energy certifier. It is not the resale of a freely transferable deduction. Establish building ownership, designer responsibility, applicable construction and placed-in-service dates, energy-model support, allocation documentation, and the rules governing the particular project year. Section 179D includes a termination rule for property whose construction begins after June 30, 2026; a current calendar date alone does not establish project eligibility. Illustratively, a $100,000 allowable deduction at a 24% marginal rate represents $24,000 of potential taxpayer benefit, while a separately agreed $6,000 documentation engagement produces only $6,000 of operator fees. Neither figure establishes the deduction without project-specific substantiation. Apply Treasury Circular 230 Section 10.27 to the actual practitioner service and proceeding, accounting for applicable judicial limits rather than assuming all tax-related contingency arrangements are permitted or prohibited. If eligibility, allocation authority, or compensation treatment remains disputed, pause allocation, obtain independent tax review, and offer fixed-fee documentation support only for eligible projects. Do not substitute a marketing success fee for that unresolved analysis.

sections.heading: 2. Install six executable reference modules around a transactional fee subledger
paragraphs: Extract the six reference cells into the filenames shown, place them together, and initialize with python runner.py recovery.db init. Python 3.9 and SQLite are sufficient; the chapter module itself imports no application dependencies. The reference is a refund-fee subledger, not a complete general ledger or a tax return engine. It deliberately excludes custodial funds, supplier principal, recurring savings accruals, credit notes, and foreign currency. Those require additional reviewed posting types rather than improvised negative receipts. Store integer cents and integer basis points, with explicit half-up fee rounding. The natural claim key combines client, invoice item, and play; make invoice_key granular enough to distinguish recoverable line items while preventing the same line from being counted twice under renamed campaigns. SHA-256 connects the database to immutable evidence retained outside it. A hash proves identity of bytes, not commercial validity, so a named reviewer still validates every document. The scoring script records facts without granting credentials. Run intake with a JSON payload containing the documented parameters; missing facts, altered replay payloads, or duplicate natural keys fail instead of silently changing an existing claim.

Every mutating function obtains BEGIN IMMEDIATE before reading mutable state, holds the SQLite writer reservation through validation and posting, and commits the event with its business effect. Unique event identifiers reject changed retries; a matching replay returns without another posting. A partial unique index allows one earnings entry per claim, and a provider-qualified external reference prevents two local claims from sharing one acknowledgement. Concurrent receipts serialize before checking the open balance, so two workers cannot each consume the same receivable. These properties remove check-then-write races within this controlled database path. Use one local database on durable storage, not a network filesystem or independent copied databases. Set foreign keys on every connection, retain FULL synchronous durability, and restrict write access to the service identity. The reference makes no network submissions: it records an acknowledgement only after a documented external action. Where a provider supports idempotency keys, reuse a stable claim identifier. Where it does not, an ambiguous timeout requires a status inquiry and human resolution, never an automatic resend. A database transaction cannot make an unrelated carrier system participate in an atomic commit.

The verification and escrow state machine starts at held, advances through verified, submitted, settled, and invoiced, and allows documented voiding before settlement. Here escrow means an internal evidence hold, not possession of client money. Submission requires a provider-qualified acknowledgement; settlement requires documentary proof that the actual customer recovery equals the reviewed amount. A partial award stops the transition for controlled rework rather than overstating fees. Invoicing records completed contractual performance and an unconditional fee right, then debits fee receivables and credits operator revenue atomically. Bank receipts debit cash and credit those receivables using an account-qualified bank transaction identifier. The minimal implementation allocates one bank transaction to one claim; multi-invoice deposits need a dedicated allocation model before use. Reconciliation shows earned fees minus allocated receipts equals remaining receivables for every claim and cohort. QA runs inside one read transaction, avoiding inconsistent snapshots during concurrent writes. Structural checks supplement, rather than replace, independent bank and source-document matching. Export monthly operator expenses into the accounting system separately; do not infer owner profit from this revenue-only subledger. These supplied modules are reference source, not reported execution results.

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claims (
    claim_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    invoice_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    play TEXT NOT NULL,
    cohort TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length(source_sha256) = 64),
    recoverable_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(recoverable_cents > 0),
    fee_bps INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(fee_bps BETWEEN 1 AND 5000),
    score INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
    state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'held'
        CHECK(state IN ('held', 'verified', 'submitted', 'settled',
                        'invoiced', 'void')),
    external_ref TEXT UNIQUE,
    UNIQUE(client_id, invoice_key, play)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    claim_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES claims(claim_id),
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    payload_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length(payload_sha256) = 64),
    evidence_json TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT
        (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS postings (
    event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES events(event_id),
    claim_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES claims(claim_id),
    debit_account TEXT NOT NULL,
    credit_account TEXT NOT NULL,
    amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(amount_cents > 0),
    CHECK(
        (debit_account = 'AR' AND credit_account = 'REVENUE')
        OR
        (debit_account = 'CASH' AND credit_account = 'AR')
    )
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS one_earning_per_claim
    ON postings(claim_id)
    WHERE credit_account = 'REVENUE';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_by_claim
    ON events(claim_id, created_at);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS postings_by_claim
    ON postings(claim_id);
Natural keys, event keys, provider references, and one earning per claim have database uniqueness enforcement.
intake.py — validate identifiers, freeze scoring inputs, and insert one work packet

import hashlib
import json
from datetime import date


def intake(db, claim_id, client_id, invoice_key, play, cohort,
           source_sha256, recoverable_cents, fee_bps, facts):
    if not all(isinstance(value, str) and value.strip()
               for value in (claim_id, client_id, invoice_key, play)):
        raise ValueError('Nonempty claim identities are required')
    if date.fromisoformat(cohort + '-01').strftime('%Y-%m') != cohort:
        raise ValueError('Use an ISO year-month cohort')
    if (len(source_sha256) != 64 or
            any(c not in '0123456789abcdef' for c in source_sha256)):
        raise ValueError('Use the immutable source SHA-256 digest')
    if type(recoverable_cents) is not int or recoverable_cents <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Recovery must be positive integer cents')
    if type(fee_bps) is not int or not 1 <= fee_bps <= 5000:
        raise ValueError('Fee basis points must be between 1 and 5000')

    weights = {
        'authorization_signed': 25,
        'baseline_locked': 25,
        'deadline_open': 20,
        'contract_eligible': 20,
        'payer_identified': 10,
    }
    if set(facts) != set(weights):
        raise ValueError('Supply every named scoring fact exactly once')
    if any(type(value) is not bool for value in facts.values()):
        raise ValueError('Scoring facts must be actual booleans')
    score = sum(weight for name, weight in weights.items() if facts[name])
    payload = {
        'claim_id': claim_id,
        'client_id': client_id,
        'invoice_key': invoice_key,
        'play': play,
        'cohort': cohort,
        'source_sha256': source_sha256,
        'recoverable_cents': recoverable_cents,
        'fee_bps': fee_bps,
        'facts': facts,
    }
    encoded = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'))
    digest = hashlib.sha256(encoded.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
    event_id = 'intake:' + claim_id
    values = (
        claim_id, client_id, invoice_key, play, cohort, source_sha256,
        recoverable_cents, fee_bps, score,
    )

    db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
    try:
        prior = db.execute(
            'SELECT payload_sha256 FROM events WHERE event_id = ?',
            (event_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if prior:
            if prior[0] != digest:
                raise ValueError('An intake key cannot change its payload')
            db.commit()
            return claim_id

        db.execute(
            'INSERT INTO claims '
            '(claim_id, client_id, invoice_key, play, cohort, source_sha256, '
            'recoverable_cents, fee_bps, score) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)',
            values,
        )
        db.execute(
            'INSERT INTO events '
            '(event_id, claim_id, kind, payload_sha256, evidence_json) '
            'VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)',
            (event_id, claim_id, 'intake', digest, encoded),
        )
        db.commit()
        return claim_id
    except BaseException:
        db.rollback()
        raise

reconciliation.sql — expose earned fees, collected cash, and remaining claim receivables

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS claim_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    c.claim_id,
    c.client_id,
    c.cohort,
    c.state,
    COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN p.credit_account = 'REVENUE'
        THEN p.amount_cents ELSE 0 END
    ), 0) AS earned_fee_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN p.debit_account = 'CASH'
        THEN p.amount_cents ELSE 0 END
    ), 0) AS received_fee_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN p.debit_account = 'AR'
        THEN p.amount_cents
        WHEN p.credit_account = 'AR'
        THEN -p.amount_cents
        ELSE 0 END
    ), 0) AS receivable_cents
FROM claims AS c
LEFT JOIN postings AS p ON p.claim_id = c.claim_id
GROUP BY c.claim_id, c.client_id, c.cohort, c.state;
Each paired posting contributes once; customer recovery principal never enters operator revenue or fee cash.

One read snapshot prevents mixed-version checks; independent bank matching remains an additional operating control.
runner.py — initialize storage and expose explicit JSON-driven operational commands

import argparse
import json
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from intake import intake
from workflow import advance, receive
from qa import check


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('database')
    parser.add_argument(
        'action',
        choices=('init', 'intake', 'advance', 'receive', 'report', 'qa'),
    )
    parser.add_argument('--payload', default='{}')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    payload = json.loads(args.payload)
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    db = sqlite3.connect(args.database, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
    try:
        db.execute('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON')
        db.execute('PRAGMA busy_timeout = 30000')
        db.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL')
        db.execute('PRAGMA synchronous = FULL')
        if args.action == 'init':
            sql = (
                (root / 'schema.sql').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
                + '\n'
                + (root / 'reconciliation.sql').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
            )
            try:
                db.executescript('BEGIN IMMEDIATE;\n' + sql + '\nCOMMIT;')
            except BaseException:
                if db.in_transaction:
                    db.rollback()
                raise
            print('Schema and reconciliation view initialized')
        elif args.action == 'intake':
            print(intake(db, **payload))
        elif args.action == 'advance':
            advance(db, **payload)
            print('Transition committed or matching replay accepted')
        elif args.action == 'receive':
            receive(db, **payload)
            print('Receipt committed or matching replay accepted')
        elif args.action == 'qa':
            print(json.dumps(check(db), sort_keys=True))
        else:
            rows = db.execute(
                'SELECT cohort, SUM(earned_fee_cents), '
                'SUM(received_fee_cents), SUM(receivable_cents) '
                'FROM claim_reconciliation GROUP BY cohort ORDER BY cohort'
            ).fetchall()
            print(json.dumps(rows))
    finally:
        db.close()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
Local durable storage, controlled writers, bounded lock waiting, and explicit errors define the supported deployment.

sop_steps.detail: A settlement mismatch must stop; a duplicate receipt must be harmless; competing receipts must never exceed the remaining receivable.

sections.heading: 3. Operate the evidence queue, specialist handoffs, and exception recovery without inventing cash
paragraphs: Run a daily queue by deadline exposure, expected collectible fee, and remaining evidence effort. The founder owns customer communication, engagement scope, and collection; three contractors cover invoice analysis, domain verification, and bookkeeping with narrowly separated access. Begin each morning with expiring carrier claims, unresolved acknowledgements, municipal inquiries, and tax-processing deadlines. An OCR exception goes back to the source invoice, not directly into a dispute letter. Utility reviewers compare billed rate components to the effective tariff and distinguish a retrospective credit from a prospective classification change. Parcel reviewers establish that service commitments applied to that shipment before calculating lateness. The bookkeeper receives accepted amounts and evidence references, not authority to revise eligibility. Hold a weekly exception review with explicit owners and next-contact dates. A municipal refund that takes another 60 days changes the collection forecast; it does not justify recording a bank receipt. Similarly, a verbal carrier concession stays out of settled status until the credit memo or payment evidence arrives. This cadence protects the small-team model by preventing contractors from repeatedly rediscovering why the same unresolved claim cannot yet move forward.

Separate tax-credit workflow from ordinary bill corrections at the first intake screen. WOTC uses employer prescreening and state workforce certification, including the statutory 28-day submission timing under Section 51(d)(13); confirm the applicable eligible-hire window under Section 51(c)(4) rather than assuming a later legislative extension. The Form 8850 process must capture the applicant's timely prescreening information, employer signatures, hiring dates, and submission evidence. An ATS integration should create a deadline task and secure document request, not fabricate answers from demographic guesses. Where tax-return information falls within Section 7216, apply its disclosure and use restrictions and the applicable Treasury regulations before sharing records with contractors or outside processors. Property-tax matters receive a separate jurisdiction review; Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1152, for example, governs property-tax consultants within its scope and exemptions. Independent qualified specialists own technical conclusions outside the founder's competence. Compensation follows the actual service and applicable rules, not the general 25%–50% commercial audit pitch. The fixed processing and documentation examples in the matrix therefore remain outside the refund-only reference ledger until their performance obligations and posting rules are explicitly implemented.

Use exception handling to preserve economics instead of concealing losses. A disputed baseline creates a measurement task; an expired deadline creates a closed loss; an unconfirmed provider response creates an inquiry, not another submission. For partial settlements, retain the original claim and evidence trail, approve a revised work packet under a controlled amendment procedure, and prevent the same provider acknowledgement from supporting duplicate revenue. The compact reference intentionally refuses this amendment path until an extended model is reviewed. Likewise, reversals, customer refunds, chargebacks, and split bank deposits belong in explicit extension tests before live use. Archive raw evidence with restricted access, encrypted storage, retention dates, and documented deletion authority; the SQLite database stores digests and review metadata rather than payroll documents. Restore a backup into an isolated environment and compare claim counts, event counts, fee totals, and bank allocations before declaring recovery successful. For shared savings, recalculate each month using agreed production or occupancy normalizers and retain the baseline version used. A 36-month contract is a measurement commitment, not permission to recognize three years of estimated fees on signing day.

sections.heading: 4. Walk a ninety-day cohort from lead scrubs to Base-case earned profit and closing cash
paragraphs: Use a deliberately explicit steady-production quarter rather than portraying a cold start as instant cash. The modeled operator begins with authorized prospect relationships, ready invoice access, $24,000 opening liquidity, and no opening fee receivables. This fits within the $6,000–$35,000 startup capital range but does not eliminate the stated one-to-four-month first-deal interval for a new entrant. Each month supplies 40 qualified leads, ten signed work packets, two eligibility scrubs, and eight retained cases. Across 90 days, 120 leads produce 30 signed packets, six closed losses, and 24 collectible cases. Cohort A earns $60,000, cohort B earns $41,250, and cohort C earns $25,000; these are different verified recovery sizes, not equal-value deals. All use a permitted 25% commercial refund fee, requiring $240,000, $165,000, and $100,000 of actual customer recoveries respectively. The resulting $505,000 customer recovery total is coincidentally equal to annual Base operator revenue, but the two measures have different periods and meanings. Quarter operator revenue is only $126,250. Scrubbed packets earn zero and their review effort remains inside the modeled delivery expense.

Month 1 recognizes $30,000 from cohort A and collects $20,000, leaving $10,000 receivable. Month 2 recognizes another $20,000 from A and $22,500 from B, while collecting $25,000 from A and $15,000 from B. Month 3 recognizes A's remaining $10,000, B's remaining $18,750, and C's $25,000; receipts are $15,000, $21,250, and $20,000 respectively. Thus quarter earnings total $126,250, cash receipts total $116,250, and closing receivables total $10,000, split evenly between B and C. Customer recovery evidence supports each recognition event, and the contract makes the fee unconditional at completed performance; a signature alone never earns revenue. The cash pattern assumes reasonably prompt commercial refund processing, not municipal or tax-refund timing. Slower utility credits move their affected cases into later periods instead of borrowing cash from another cohort in the presentation. The two scrubs per cohort consist of one contract or eligibility failure and one evidence or deadline failure. Their losses reduce signed-to-retained conversion to 80%, with no invented fee receivable to write off afterward.

Monthly operating expense is $23,987.50, comprising $6,500 of recurring overhead and $17,487.50 of delivery, contractor, and variable operating costs. Recurring overhead stays within the supplied $1,500–$9,500 monthly opex range; the additional direct costs reconcile the full scorecard expense envelope rather than pretending the overhead range covers every expense. Quarter costs are $71,962.50 and earned owner profit is $54,287.50, exactly 43% of revenue. Cash operating flow is negative $3,987.50 in Month 1, positive $16,012.50 in Month 2, and positive $32,262.50 in Month 3. Cumulative flow therefore reaches $44,287.50, with $68,287.50 closing cash after opening liquidity. The $10,000 difference between earned profit and cash flow is closing receivables. No owner distributions, capital purchases, borrowing, or personal taxes enter this operating illustration. Four equivalent quarters produce $505,000 revenue, $287,850 expenses, and $217,150 annual owner profit with one full-time operator and three contractors. Annual cash requires its own receivable roll-forward; do not multiply the first quarter's collection lag mechanically. Conservative and Scaled economics remain separate canonical cases, not extrapolations from optimistic recovery principal or unsigned savings estimates.
