sections.heading: 1. Build an eighteen-source directory that separates signals from evidence
paragraphs: Start with a source register, not a purchased prospect list. The eighteen directory entries across this section and the next distinguish public discovery from account-authorized evidence. Each connector records its owner, permitted purpose, access route, fee arrangement, observed publication delay, retrieval timestamp, and fallback. Refresh schedules below are desk polling policies, not promises that agencies publish on those schedules. Attach the source URL, document date, effective period, content hash, and retrieval identity to every download. A county assessment roll can identify a large warehouse, but it cannot establish its parcel-carrier account, contracted service guarantee, utility rider, or eligible employees. Resolve the parcel owner through the county assessor and the relevant Secretary of State business search; then ask the actual operating company for account documents under signed authority. Do not equate a registered agent with the purchasing decision maker. Preserve both public entity identifiers and customer-confirmed account identifiers, because landlords, tenants, management companies, and payroll entities often differ. That identity discipline prevents a plausible prospect from becoming an unauthorized claim. Before disclosing account-specific tariff or refund findings, secure the Letter of Authorization and a dated invoice baseline covering the relevant service period.

Use twelve explicit operating lanes: parcel service-guarantee recovery, parcel duplicate-charge recovery, parcel accessorial correction, utility tariff reclassification, utility meter-error recovery, cooling-tower sewer deductions, waste-service right-sizing, telecom inventory recovery, property-assessment appeals, WOTC processing, historic and brownfield credit screening, and transferable_tax_credit_brokerage_syndication. These are twelve mapped plays, not twelve separate revenue assumptions. Give each lane its own evidence requirements, filing clock, and fee trigger. The first six can share invoice normalization, while WOTC needs restricted employee records and credit transactions need project-specific tax documentation. Public utility tariff libraries reveal rider changes; municipal sewer ordinances establish whether a qualifying deduction exists; county records provide assessment history rather than an automatic appeal valuation. For an illustrative utility screen, 400,000 billed kWh multiplied by a suspected $0.012 rate difference produces a $4,800 investigation lead. A verified, issued $4,800 refund at a 35% contracted share produces $1,680 of operator revenue. If demand charges or rider eligibility eliminate the difference, close the lead without booking revenue. Store that rejected hypothesis so the next analyst does not rediscover it. Treat vacancy, ownership changes, and service addresses as routing clues, never substitutes for measured usage or the governing account contract.

Energy-project origination requires a correction to a common sourcing shortcut: DOE and EPA are not universal interconnection-queue operators. Berkeley Lab's Queued Up compilation supplies periodically published market context, while the relevant ISO, RTO, or utility maintains the underlying queue. EPA ECHO supplies facility and environmental records, not proof of transferable credit eligibility. FERC eLibrary provides relevant filings, but a filing does not establish placed-in-service status or a usable tax basis. Join projects using queue identifiers, legal entities, locations, and documented ownership chains rather than project names alone. State film offices and historic-preservation records support different statutes and different transfer mechanics; never put them through an IRC § 6418 calculator merely because both involve credits. An illustrative 100-project batch with 20 documented operating projects and five sellers willing to share records yields five diligence files, not five saleable credits. If the originating registry stops publishing or prohibits automated extraction, use permitted downloads and direct document requests. Cache unchanged files, honor published access conditions, and record manual collection dates. This makes public-record research reproducible without pretending that a stale directory constitutes transaction-ready inventory. Preserve rejected entity matches alongside accepted ones to expose mistaken joins during review.

sections.heading: 2. Connect authorized billing rails without inventing refund APIs
paragraphs: Carrier developer accounts are not blanket access to billing adjustments. FedEx and UPS expose documented services, but available refund, invoice, and claim functions depend on product, account, geography, entitlement, and current contractual terms. Read the current documentation with the customer's authorized account administrator; record supported endpoints and explicitly mark unsupported workflows as manual tasks. Do not assume that a loss-and-damage claims API also processes service-guarantee requests. For account-authorized EDI, request the carrier's implementation guide and validate its supported transaction format; X12 210 is relevant where offered, not a universal parcel billing feed. A desk examining 10,000 shipments might flag 300 late events, then retain only 120 after service commitments, exclusions, and account waivers are applied. At $18 average eligible charges, the resulting $2,160 recovery opportunity yields $864 at a 40% share only when the contractual earning condition is satisfied. Preserve shipment identifiers, promised and actual delivery timestamps, time zones, service levels, and waiver evidence. If a service endpoint fails, switch to authorized portal exports and queue submission tasks against the actual filing deadline. Tracking events support investigation; they do not independently prove a refundable billed amount. Never resubmit a request merely because the first response timed out.

Enrichment should follow a cheap-to-expensive waterfall. Begin with the customer's account roster, then public parcel and entity records, then verified billing contacts, and only then a licensed commercial contact provider when its terms permit the use. Retain the provider, retrieval date, matching basis, and deletion requirements; do not enrich WOTC applicant records with unrelated marketing attributes. For utilities, Green Button interval data can reveal load patterns, while ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager provides benchmarking context. Neither replaces the billed tariff, meter multiplier, demand ratchet, taxes, or approved sewer deduction. An illustrative 2,000,000 gallons of documented cooling-tower evaporation at a qualifying $7 per thousand gallons suggests $14,000 of avoided sewer charges. Meter approval dates and local rules may reduce that amount to zero for earlier periods. At a 30% earned share, $14,000 of accepted benefit supports $4,200 of operator revenue. When interval feeds lag, reconcile monthly bills and postpone interval-based conclusions rather than filling gaps with invented consumption. Keep provider processing lag separate from meter-read dates so analysts can distinguish delayed delivery from genuinely missing measurements. Use customer-approved engineering records when portal data cannot resolve the physical system boundary.

WOTC connectors need a different trust boundary from expense auditing. Under IRC § 51(d)(13), the certification workflow includes a pre-screening notice completed on or before the employment offer and submission to the designated local agency within 28 days after work begins. Form 8850 and the applicable ETA documentation must follow current instructions; an ATS timestamp alone does not establish eligibility. The last established federal authorization covered qualifying hires through December 31, 2025, so verify any subsequent extension before offering credits for later hires. An illustrative standard eligible employee with $6,000 of qualifying wages and at least 400 hours produces a $2,400 credit at 40%, subject to category-specific rules and other restrictions. A contracted $120 processing charge is desk revenue; the $2,400 employer credit is not. Missing timely pre-screening or certification submission cannot be repaired by altering timestamps. Retain the documented exception and have the responsible specialist determine available treatment. Scope ATS permissions to required fields, restrict sensitive responses, and use state portal acknowledgments as submission evidence. Review fee structure under Treasury Circular 230 § 10.27 wherever covered tax services are involved rather than copying a utility contingency agreement.

sections.heading: 3. Turn raw records into a reproducible claim ledger
paragraphs: Build the pipeline around immutable evidence and explicit transformations. Store original PDFs, CSV files, EDI payloads, and API responses separately from normalized tables. A practical small-desk implementation uses an encrypted object store, PostgreSQL for multiuser records, and SQLite for isolated analyst workbooks; none is a substitute for access control or tested backups. Python's csv, decimal, hashlib, json, sqlite3, and zoneinfo modules cover essential parsing, money calculations, hashing, and timestamps. Use Decimal values with explicit currency and rounding rules rather than binary floating-point amounts. For image-only invoices, Tesseract and OCRmyPDF are optional external tools, while pdftotext extracts existing text layers without reinterpreting images. Record tool versions and page coordinates for every extracted amount. Require invoice totals to reconcile to line items, taxes, adjustments, and credits before generating claim candidates. An illustrative batch of 1,000 invoices with 40 extraction exceptions needs a forty-item review queue, not silent deletion of those records. When OCR confuses a meter identifier or decimal separator, retain the original image and request human confirmation. Only confirmed fields should enter a recoverable-amount calculation; confidence scores prioritize review but do not authorize claims. Preserve each correction as a versioned event with its reviewer and rationale.

Create four linked ledgers: source evidence, claim candidates, submissions, and cash realization. The evidence ledger holds immutable file hashes and provenance; candidates hold the rule version and proposed adjustment; submissions hold the actual external acknowledgment; cash realization holds remittance references and the fee allocation. Use a business key such as account, invoice, charge line, reason code, and service period to prevent duplicate recovery attempts. A network timeout changes a submission to reconciliation required, not automatically to failed. Check the carrier or agency record before retrying. Model status transitions explicitly so an analyst cannot jump from suspected overcharge to earned fee. For shared savings, compare the accepted counterfactual with actual normalized consumption, approved rates, and contract exclusions. A $500 monthly verified reduction over 36 months creates $18,000 of client benefit and $5,400 at a 30% share, but billing and recognition follow the contract and applicable accounting treatment rather than booking the entire benefit immediately. If operations change, pause the affected savings calculation and rebuild the baseline. Keep client acknowledgments, rate-change dates, and measurement assumptions alongside the calculation, because those records resolve most fee disputes more effectively than a polished dashboard.

Diagnostics should expose economic failure before throughput rises. Track source freshness, rejected joins, invoice reconciliation errors, deadline coverage, submission duplicates, denial reasons, cash aging, and collected fees per reviewer hour. Split each metric by play and counterparty; a utility refund backlog should not hide behind fast parcel credits. An illustrative week with $12,000 of proposed refunds, $7,000 accepted, and $4,000 issued produces distinct proposed, accepted, and cash figures. At a 35% fee payable on issued refunds, the immediately billable amount is $1,400, subject to the agreement. Report the remaining amounts as pipeline states, not revenue. Restrict payroll and WOTC documents to their own role group, encrypt credentials outside workbooks, redact sensitive identifiers from logs, and test restoration from backup. Retention rules should distinguish statutory substantiation, contractual evidence, and short-lived contact enrichment. A deletion request must not silently erase records subject to an applicable retention obligation; route the conflict to the responsible records owner. If a connector loses authority, stop collection and preserve existing evidence according to the governing terms. Favor a manually verified ten-claim batch over an unattended thousand-claim batch with unresolved identity errors.

sections.heading: 4. Structure credit origination correctly and preserve scorecard economics
paragraphs: The mapped play transferable_tax_credit_brokerage_syndication belongs to TRACK_1 and needs separate transaction logic. For eligible federal credits under IRC § 6418, a transferee cannot subsequently transfer the purchased credit; a broker therefore cannot buy title at $0.85 and resell that same credit at $0.94. Structure a direct eligible-taxpayer-to-buyer transfer with separately documented intermediary compensation, or decline the proposed structure. State film, historic rehabilitation, and brownfield programs require their own statutory eligibility and transfer analysis. At $1,000,000 face value, the proposed seller pricing range of $0.82–$0.88 implies $820,000–$880,000, while buyer pricing of $0.92–$0.96 implies $920,000–$960,000. The arithmetic difference ranges from $40,000 to $140,000 before transaction costs, but it is not automatically an available or lawful brokerage fee. A $0.85 seller reference and $0.94 buyer reference imply $90,000 of gross economic room; illustrative $20,000 insurance, $15,000 diligence, and $10,000 escrow and other costs leave $45,000 before remaining expenses. Have specialists establish which payments constitute transfer consideration, service compensation, or buyer costs, and allocate every dollar explicitly. Never describe a spread calculation as a completed transaction or recognized revenue before contracts and tax treatment support it.

Source-credit verification starts with the eligible taxpayer, project ownership, credit type, tax year, calculation workpapers, placed-in-service evidence, and applicable labor or bonus-credit substantiation. Federal pre-filing registration through IRS Energy Credits Online supplies registration numbers; it does not certify the substantive credit amount. Verify the buyer's capacity to use the credit, including limitations relevant to individuals; a high-net-worth prospect is not automatically an eligible economic buyer for every project. The stipulated fallback is no unhedged balance-sheet inventory and simultaneous back-to-back escrow funded by the buyer's wire, with bound non-cancelable tax-credit insurance. For federal transfers, that describes coordinated funding and documents, not successive credit ownership. Require the insurer's actual cancellation terms, covered risks, exclusions, limits, retention, and claims process; the label alone establishes nothing. If the required coverage or simultaneous structure cannot be secured, do not close. Insurance does not cure an ineligible credit or erase statutory recapture and excessive-transfer exposure. Model seller indemnity collectibility separately from insured recovery. Keep escrow release instructions conditional on executed documents, verified funding, and the agreed evidence package, while leaving return elections and filing requirements with the responsible taxpayers and their authorized advisers.

Keep these transaction illustrations outside the canonical volume scorecard unless their earned fees are expressly included in the existing revenue envelope. Formula v2.0 fixes Conservative operator revenue at $110,000, expenses at $77,000, and owner net profit at $33,000; Base revenue is $505,000, expenses are $287,850, and profit is $217,150; Scaled revenue is $900,000, expenses are $396,000, and profit is $504,000. The resulting margins are 30%, 43.0%, and 56%, with teams of 1 FT plus 3 contractors, 1 FT plus 3 contractors, and 2 FT plus 4 contractors respectively. Client utility spending, parcel charges, credit face value, and escrow wires remain outside operator revenue. Where the desk acts as agent, apply the appropriate ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis and retain only its earned service consideration; do not apply another blanket retained-share haircut to scorecard figures already stated as operator fees. Startup capital remains $6,000–$35,000 and monthly operating overhead $1,500–$9,500, with total scenario expenses also covering delivery costs beyond that overhead range. Assign specialist capacity before buying more leads: carrier waivers, municipal refund delays, tax substantiation, and local consultant licensing are the throughput constraints that software cannot simply remove.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #38, Rank #06 of 42, earns a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score by turning documented billing errors and eligible incentives into earned operator fees across 12 mapped plays. The operating boundary is precise: carrier recoveries, utility adjustments, assessment appeals, federal tax work, and state credit placements require different authority, pricing, and evidence. Secure signed authorization and baseline invoices before revealing findings; separate restricted tax engagements from commercial contingency work. Formula v2.0 projects annual owner net profit of $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled. This chapter supplies contract mechanics, state-specific credential checks, transferable-credit settlement controls, and verbatim scripts that sell an auditable process without promising recovery amounts or treating client refunds as operator revenue.

sections.heading: 1. Assign Each Recovery Lane Its Own Authority and Fee Rule
paragraphs: Build twelve operating lanes before quoting one blended contingency: FedEx parcel refunds, UPS parcel refunds, utility tariff corrections, utility sales-tax refunds, cooling-tower sewer credits, waste invoice recoveries, telecom billing disputes, property assessment appeals, WOTC processing, specialty federal credit substantiation, 36-month shared-savings administration, and state transferable-credit placement. These are the chapter's twelve mapped plays, not twelve interchangeable permissions. Commercial invoice analysis does not authorize tax representation, a property appeal, or credential sharing. Create a jurisdiction register recording the client entity, service address, taxing authority, carrier account, claim period, limitation date, permitted representative, and applicable fee restriction. For FedEx and UPS, obtain signed Letters of Authorization and baseline invoice snapshots before disclosing shipment-level findings. Inspect the customer's negotiated agreement for service-guarantee waivers, claim exclusions, and duplicate-recovery provisions. A documented late shipment is an investigative lead, not automatically an eligible refund. For utilities, distinguish tariff misapplication from an engineering retrofit and separate historical refunds from prospective rate changes. Waste and telecom claims turn on service orders, renewal terms, usage records, taxes, and dispute deadlines. Freeze the original source documents with collection dates and hashes so another reviewer can reproduce the conclusion after the supplier changes its portal or invoice format.

Treasury Circular 230, 31 CFR §10.27, restricts practitioner contingent fees for covered matters before the IRS, subject to defined exceptions and relevant judicial limits. Do not translate a carrier's thirty-percent recovery arrangement into a percentage of a federal credit merely because both engagements produce cash. Section 10.27 distinguishes ordinary return work from specified examination, interest-or-penalty refund, and judicial proceeding circumstances; court decisions also limit its application in certain settings. Have the responsible tax practitioner classify the actual service and document the permissible pricing basis rather than asserting a universal percentage-fee exemption. Use a separate fixed-fee or hourly engagement when the proposed contingency is restricted. Under 31 CFR §10.22, covered practitioners must exercise due diligence; attaching software output does not discharge that responsibility. WOTC introduces a different clock: 26 U.S.C. §51(d)(13) requires timely prescreening and certification procedures, including submission within the statutory twenty-eight-day period when using that route. The provision in §51(c)(4) sets a commencement-of-work cutoff of December 31, 2025 unless subsequently amended. For later starts, verify enacted extension language before representing eligibility, while continuing properly supported work on earlier qualifying starts. Never backdate prescreening records to repair a missed deadline.

Property-tax engagements need a state-by-state credential map, not a national consultant label. Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1152 regulates property-tax consultants and provides specific exemptions; determine whether the actual person performing the work must register and whether supervision requirements apply. California Revenue and Taxation Code §1607 addresses written authorization for agents appearing in assessment proceedings. Neither example establishes permission for every state, tribunal, or court appeal. Record who may inspect records, sign the application, negotiate, appear, and litigate; retain local counsel where the next procedural step requires an attorney. For utility and sewer claims, retrieve the applicable commission tariff or municipal ordinance, including meter certification, retroactivity, and refund-interest rules. A cooling-tower deduction may require an approved deduct meter rather than an estimated evaporation spreadsheet. Utility sales-tax exemptions belong in a separate state tax workstream because certificate requirements and refund claimants differ. Carrier API access must follow the account owner's authorization and the provider's developer agreement; an EDI invoice feed does not establish claim-submission rights. When authority is incomplete, keep the engagement in read-only analysis, identify the missing credential or document, and pause submission without allowing a filing deadline to disappear from the task register.

callout.body: The submission owner records evidence for each check, names the responsible reviewer, and preserves the decision with the claim packet.
items: Match the signed Letter of Authorization to the exact legal entity, account numbers, permitted actions, expiration, and provider requirements.

sections.heading: 2. Draft Separate Schedules for Scope, Earnings, Data, and Exit
paragraphs: Use a master services agreement with lane-specific schedules rather than a single promise to recover every overpayment. The scope schedule names covered entities, accounts, periods, taxes, suppliers, claim types, and exclusions; its attachment freezes the baseline invoice inventory before findings are disclosed. The authorization schedule permits only specified acts, such as retrieving invoices and submitting supported billing disputes, and separately addresses settlement authority. It does not give the operator ownership of client refunds or power to change banking instructions. Define a recovery as cleared cash or an actually applied account credit, net of reversals and agreed offsets, rather than an issued claim number. At a thirty-percent fee, a $20,000 accepted claim that yields $18,000 cash and a $2,000 rejection earns $5,400, not $6,000. Specify invoicing dates, payment terms, credit verification, reversal adjustments, and collection responsibility. Separate any fixed WOTC processing charge from commercial refund shares and from restricted federal tax services. Have the client pay each supplier normally while disputes proceed unless the supplier expressly authorizes another arrangement. An auditor-created payment shortfall can trigger service interruption, late charges, or an avoidable dispute over the operator's own fee.

For 36-month shared savings, attach a measurement formula that neutralizes usage, weather, occupancy, service level, and tariff movements where relevant. A $5,000 monthly baseline reduced to $4,000 at equivalent activity supports $1,000 verified monthly savings; a thirty-percent split produces $300 per month and $10,800 over thirty-six fully realized months. Those future installments are not automatically current revenue. Define the commencement date, comparison period, verification source, treatment of facility closures, and whether negotiated extensions require a fresh signature. Prevent double billing when a historical refund and a future rate correction address the same charge. Anti-circumvention language should protect identified findings and documented introductions for a defined period, with exclusions for preexisting projects and independently documented discoveries. It should not claim every future improvement across the client's business. Require a dated findings register and client acknowledgment rather than relying on a broad confidentiality sentence. A termination schedule distinguishes earned fees, pending authorized claims, prospective work, and a narrowly defined collection tail. State who completes deadline-sensitive filings after termination, whether the client may revoke portal access immediately, and how both parties exchange the evidence needed to avoid duplicate claims or abandoned appeals.

Negotiate liability, dispute resolution, and information rights as operating mechanics, not decorative boilerplate. A liability cap can reference a defined amount or specified fee period, with negotiated treatment of fraud, willful misconduct, confidentiality breaches, and other appropriate exceptions; enforceability depends on governing law and the actual claim. Specify required insurance, notice procedures, mitigation duties, and responsibility for penalties caused by inaccurate client records versus operator errors. The dispute clause identifies governing law, venue or arbitration rules, escalation contacts, and treatment of undisputed invoices. It cannot extend a statutory appeal deadline or prevent a regulator from exercising authority. Give the client ownership of its invoices, payroll records, claim packets, and engagement-specific deliverables, while reserving the operator's preexisting methods and reusable software. Permit use of confidential records only for contracted purposes and identify approved subprocessors. Establish access controls, incident notification timing, export formats, retention periods, and deletion obligations subject to applicable preservation duties. IRS Form 2848 and Form 8821 serve different purposes; information access is not equivalent to representation authority. Tax-return information may implicate 26 U.S.C. §7216 and implementing regulations when handled by covered preparers, so data reuse and disclosures require a separate, fact-specific review.

sections.heading: 3. Settle Transferable Credits Without Misstating Value or Revenue
paragraphs: The play state_film_historic_brownfield_tax_credit_brokerage, TRACK_1, matches certified state film, historic rehabilitation, and brownfield credits with eligible taxpayers at negotiated discounts while retaining disclosed placement fees. Transferability belongs to the particular state program and credit vintage; a label resembling a transferable program elsewhere proves nothing. Federal historic rehabilitation credits under 26 U.S.C. §47 cannot simply be sold outright because a state historic credit permits assignment. Establish statutory transfer permission, seller ownership, certification status, permitted transfer count, transfer registration, buyer eligibility, tax type, carryforward, expiration, and recapture exposure before circulating a priced opportunity. Georgia's film-credit framework in O.C.G.A. §48-7-40.26 illustrates why the actual state provision matters, but its mechanics must not be copied onto another state's historic or brownfield program. Distinguish an application from an allocation, an allocation from a final certificate, and a certificate from a completed transfer. Build the buyer list around verified tax usability, not merely corporate size. Obtain qualified state tax review and examine whether the proposed structure introduces additional licensing obligations, especially when someone proposes selling an entity interest instead of assigning a credit. A placement operator earns for documented intermediation, not for issuing a tax opinion or promising the purchaser's ultimate result.

Use transparent settlement arithmetic. In an illustrative placement, $100,000 of certified state credit face value sells for $90,000, and the seller pays a disclosed three-percent fee on purchase price. The operator earns $2,700; the seller receives $87,300 before other costs; the purchaser pays $90,000 before its own costs. The $100,000 face amount and $90,000 settlement proceeds are not operator revenue. A nominal $10,000 purchaser discount is not established realized tax savings until eligibility, usability, timing, and costs are resolved. State clearly whether the fee is seller-paid, buyer-paid, or split, and disclose any compensation from both sides before engagement. Use an independent settlement provider where appropriate, confirm bank instructions through a known contact, and release funds only against the agreed transfer evidence. The purchase agreement allocates title warranties, recapture responsibility, indemnity limits, survival periods, and dispute procedures without treating contractual promises as substitutes for statutory eligibility. If certification is defective, buyer usability fails, or transfer registration stalls, suspend settlement under the diligence contingencies. Rematch only verified eligible credits without guaranteeing tax savings. Keep a failed placement out of earned revenue and return funds according to the documented settlement instructions rather than improvising custody arrangements.

Maintain separate operating ledgers for refund shares, shared-savings installments, processing fees, and placement fees, then reconcile their earned totals to the scorecard. Formula v2.0 fixes Conservative revenue at $110,000 with $77,000 expenses and $33,000 owner net profit; Base revenue at $505,000 with $287,850 expenses and $217,150 profit; and Scaled revenue at $900,000 with $396,000 expenses and $504,000 profit. The corresponding margins are thirty percent, 43.0 percent, and fifty-six percent. Staffing remains one full-time operator plus three contractors for Conservative and Base, then two full-time operators plus four contractors for Scaled. These are canonical annual cases, not promises that a particular contract mix will achieve them. The placement example explains a fee unit without adding revenue to those totals. Under an ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis, evaluate the promised service and control before recognizing gross amounts; customer refunds and credit purchase proceeds never become operator sales merely by passing through an account. If settlement documents show gross billings, bridge them explicitly to the operator's retained share and assess variable-consideration constraints. Age municipal refund receivables separately from earned fees, because slow issuance affects collection timing and working capital even when the underlying claim is valid.

sections.heading: 4. Use Verbatim Outreach That Sells Evidence Before Outcomes
paragraphs: Commercial outreach must identify the sender, describe the actual service, and avoid invented findings. Under CAN-SPAM, 15 U.S.C. §7704, business email is not categorically exempt: use accurate routing information and subjects, required commercial identification, a valid physical postal address, and an effective opt-out honored within ten business days. Keep the suppression list operative across contractors. Use this opening verbatim after supplying the sender's normal identifying signature: 'Subject: Review of parcel and utility billing terms. We audit corporate parcel and utility invoices for documented billing errors and eligible contractual adjustments. We have not reviewed your accounts and cannot state that money is owed. For eligible commercial recovery work, our fee is an agreed share of realized recoveries. Would you consider a fifteen-minute scope call before sharing any records? This is a commercial solicitation. Reply stop to end these emails.' Append the firm's real postal address before sending. For calls and texts, classify the recipient number, technology, message purpose, consent evidence, and applicable state restrictions under the TCPA and FCC rules. Prefer individually initiated business calls with accurate identification, but do not assume that method removes every restriction. Honor a recipient's stop request immediately across the outreach sequence.

Use discovery to establish authority and constraints before discussing a recovery estimate: 'Which legal entity owns these accounts, who may authorize records access, and are another auditor or existing refund service already working on them? Can we review the carrier amendments and baseline invoices after signing the scope and authorization? We will identify exclusions before calculating any fee opportunity.' For utilities, add: 'Which meters serve production, irrigation, and cooling equipment, and has the municipality approved any sewer deduction? We need the operative tariff and meter evidence before asserting an overcharge.' For tax work, say: 'Our commercial refund percentage does not automatically apply to federal tax services. The responsible practitioner will define the service, fee basis, and filing authority before work begins.' For WOTC, ask: 'What are the employment start dates, when was prescreening completed, and which state workforce agency received each request? We verify the applicable statutory employment window before offering processing.' Do not solicit full Social Security numbers through email or a sales form. Move sensitive documentation into the approved restricted workspace after authorization. Record the prospect's answers as unverified statements until documents substantiate them; a salesperson's transcript must not silently become an eligibility determination.

For state credit placement, use: 'We introduce verified eligible state credits to purchasers whose tax position supports their use. Availability, transferability, price, and usability depend on the program and diligence. Our disclosed placement fee is separate from credit face value. We can exchange a redacted certificate summary before either party commits to settlement.' If asked for certainty, answer: 'We can commit to the documented review and settlement process, not to a tax outcome. If a diligence condition fails, settlement pauses and we consider only verified eligible alternatives.' For an account-access objection, say: 'We do not need your personal password. We can begin with authorized exports and request provider-supported access only within the signed scope.' Close discovery with a specific next step: 'Please designate the account owner, confirm existing auditor commitments, and review the proposed authorization and fee schedule. We will return a scoped evidence request before disclosing account-level findings.' Track outreach source, suppression status, authorization, qualification, document completeness, and submission readiness separately. Review a sample of sent messages weekly for unsupported savings claims, misleading government affiliation, and missing opt-outs. Measure signed qualified engagements and collected earned fees rather than inflating performance with client bill totals, credit face values, or unsubmitted recovery estimates.

sections.heading: 1. Build one evidence spine for twelve recovery plays
paragraphs: Start with a signed Letter of Authorization, a scoped service agreement, and an immutable baseline invoice snapshot before disclosing account-specific tariff or refund findings. The owner controls engagement acceptance, pricing, and final release; three contractors own parcel analysis, utility and property research, and credentialed tax-credit work respectively, with external specialists added only through explicit scopes. A Python intake service accepts authorized exports or signed webhooks and creates a tenant-scoped case identifier. Use hashlib.sha256 for source fingerprints, decimal.Decimal for money, zoneinfo for local deadlines, and sqlite3 for a single-worker pilot ledger. At higher concurrency, replace the pilot ledger with a transactional queue and database rather than sharing a writable file across machines. Store originals separately from extracted fields; every amount needs document identifier, page or record location, currency, service period, account, and extraction version. A language model receives only the minimum permitted document excerpt and returns constrained fields plus source locations. It cannot authorize access, invent a tariff, determine tax eligibility, or release a filing. Treat instructions embedded in invoices as untrusted document content. The deterministic validator rejects missing provenance and arithmetic mismatches before the case reaches a specialist. This spine makes automation transferable without confusing a faster extraction with a defensible recovery.

Use twelve explicitly named operating lanes, not twelve disconnected applications. The first seven are parcel service-guarantee refunds, parcel invoice adjustments, utility tariff corrections, cooling-tower sewer credits, waste contract savings, telecom contract savings, and property-assessment appeals. These are chapter-local mappings rather than invented identifiers from an external play catalog. For service-guarantee work, forty accepted $20 refunds at a 35% fee generate $280 of operator revenue; the $800 refunded belongs to the client. Twelve accepted $50 billing adjustments at the same percentage generate another $210, provided they are different charges. A $2,000 utility recovery at 30% earns $600, while a $3,000 sewer credit earns $900. Waste savings of $500 monthly produce $5,400 over thirty-six verified months at 30%; telecom savings of $400 monthly produce $4,320 over the same term. Neither thirty-six-month total becomes immediate earned revenue merely because a contract is signed. A permitted property appeal producing $10,000 of realized tax reduction supports a $2,500 fee at 25%, subject to the engagement and local licensing rules. Version each baseline and exclude tax-rate changes, occupancy shifts, overlapping refunds, and unimplemented recommendations from credited savings. The same source expense can support several diagnostic tests, but never multiple incompatible recovery invoices.

The remaining lanes are ATS-integrated WOTC processing, specialty-credit substantiation, b2b_class_action_contingency_recovery, duplicate vendor-payment recovery, and shared-savings verification servicing. For WOTC, twenty completed, contractually billable processing cases at $100 produce $2,000; employer credits are separate and certification does not by itself establish the final credit amount. Six specialty-credit evidence reviews at a fixed $250 produce $1,500 only when the contracted reviews are delivered. Use that fixed-fee route where a proposed contingent tax arrangement is restricted; do not camouflage a credit-based fee as processing. A verified $12,000 settlement distribution at 25% produces $3,000, and a recovered $4,000 duplicate payment at 25% produces $1,000. Savings servicing on $1,000 of verified monthly savings at 30% generates $300 for that month. When servicing implements an existing waste or telecom split, that $300 is the same revenue stream, not an additional charge. All these figures are illustrative lane economics, not additive forecasts or replacements for the canonical scorecard. The event envelope records lane, client authority, deadline, contractual fee basis, and overlapping-charge identifiers. A routing rule then assigns the required credential and submission channel. Unsupported channels fall back to documented manual processing; missing authority stops the case rather than prompting a worker to improvise access.

callout.body: The highest-value automation usually removes avoidable disputes rather than producing more speculative claims.

sections.heading: 2. Automate extraction and routing without automating entitlement
paragraphs: For FedEx and UPS, distinguish authorized invoice or tracking access from permission to submit refund claims. An EDI feed can provide billing records without exposing a public refund endpoint; a tracking API does not establish filing rights. Configure only the carrier interfaces actually granted to the client or authorized agent, and send unsupported submissions through the accepted portal or documented manual channel. Persist account, tracking number, service date, charge identifier, and claim reason as an idempotency key. A Python worker first checks contractual guarantee waivers, service exclusions, filing windows, and prior credits, then calculates the candidate amount with Decimal. The model may classify invoice descriptions but cannot infer delivery commitments from marketing language. A reviewer compares every proposed claim with source evidence before releasing a batch. Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter for transient failures, respect carrier rate limits, and stop retries on revoked authorization or permanent validation errors. A network timeout after submission is an uncertain outcome, not proof of failure. Query status or reconcile acknowledgments before retrying, otherwise a well-intentioned queue creates duplicate claims. Daily reconciliation links submitted, accepted, rejected, credited, and invoiced states. Only the credited result and applicable engagement terms support the downstream fee event; estimated refunds remain operational forecasts.

Utility automation begins with a tariff registry keyed by jurisdiction, utility, service class, effective date, and authoritative source document. OCR extracts meter readings, demand, consumption, riders, taxes, and billing intervals; deterministic checks recompute totals and flag unexpected units. A cooling-tower meter reading in gallons cannot be compared directly with billed hundred-cubic-foot units without an explicit conversion and period alignment. Retain photographs and original scans because a visually plausible OCR result can still swap a meter identifier or decimal point. Use confidence thresholds calibrated on reviewed invoices rather than trusting a vendor's score across every document type. Low confidence, a changed tariff, a meter rollover, or a newly appearing rider routes the account to the utility specialist. For waste and telecom, normalize quantities before comparing prices, then subtract implementation expenses and termination charges according to the agreement. Municipal refund issuance can lag an approved adjustment, so maintain separate approved, posted, paid, and fee-collected dates. An account credit may satisfy the contract's recovery definition even when no check arrives; establish that treatment before filing. If the tariff archive is unavailable, suspend recommendation generation and retain the case for manual research. Do not substitute a neighboring municipality's schedule or ask a model to reconstruct missing rates from memory.

ATS-integrated Form 8850 processing needs deadline engineering before model engineering. Under 26 U.S.C. §51(d)(13), the prescreening notice generally must be completed on or before the employment offer, with the certification request submitted to the designated local agency within twenty-eight days after work begins. Track offer, prescreening, start, submission, and acknowledgment timestamps separately; a start-date webhook alone cannot establish timely prescreening. Verify the statute's applicable hiring period and any enacted extension before accepting a cohort, especially for starts after December 31, 2025. Never assume authorization continues because an ATS integration still works. The worker can request missing fields, prepare forms, calculate reminders, and reconcile agency acknowledgments, but must not invent targeted-group eligibility or backdate signatures. A specialist reviews certification evidence, qualified wages, retention periods, and interaction with other credits before tax use. Circular 230 §10.27 requires engagement-specific fee analysis; ordinary parcel contingency economics cannot simply be copied onto federal tax-return work. Where tax-preparer information is involved, assess 26 U.S.C. §7216 before disclosure to an outside model or marketing service. Use restricted processing or a manual workflow when the proposed disclosure lacks an applicable basis. An expired webhook credential triggers an ATS export reconciliation, not an assumption that no hires occurred.

sections.heading: 3. Measure automation economics and keep claims evidence-first
paragraphs: Define the automation denominator before reporting a percentage. Build a fixed inventory of repetitive research, qualification, fulfillment, and acquisition tasks, with task boundaries and completion criteria frozen for each measurement period. In an illustrative thousand-task sample, 740 completed without human intervention and 260 required a person, producing 74% task automation. Do not relabel one manual review as ten automated subtasks halfway through the month. Track minutes separately because automated document routing and specialist eligibility review carry different labor weights. A second, independent thousand-run cost sample can budget $0.10 for intake and storage, $0.02 for OCR, $0.03 for model extraction, $0.01 for queue execution, and $0.04 for expected retries per run. That is $0.20 in machine cost. If 15% of runs require six minutes of review at $45 hourly, expected review cost is $0.675 per run, producing $0.875 total or $875 for the sample. These are workload assumptions, not supplier quotations, and exclude acquisition, specialist filing, owner oversight, and fixed infrastructure. Every consequential release still requires human review even when most upstream runs do not. Measure accepted findings, rejected claims, correction minutes, and realized fee collection alongside throughput. An inexpensive run that creates an unsupported filing is not productive automation.

Keep the canonical scenarios intact while using unit economics to identify bottlenecks. Conservative revenue is $110,000, with $77,000 of implied total costs and $33,000 owner profit at 30%. Base revenue is $505,000, with $287,850 of implied costs and $217,150 owner profit at 43.0%. Scaled revenue is $900,000, with $396,000 of implied costs and $504,000 owner profit at 56%. The first two cases use one full-time owner and three contractors; Scaled uses two full-time people and four contractors. These implied costs include the total expense envelope, so do not add the illustrative automation budget again without changing another cost line. The revenue basis is earned operator contingency shares, earned shared-savings splits, and processing fees, excluding underlying bills, employer credits, client refunds, and settlement principal. A 30% share of a $10,000 client recovery produces $3,000 operator revenue, not $10,000 followed by an invented revenue haircut. There is no additional retained-share multiplier supplied for this scorecard. Evaluate ASC 606 principal-versus-agent presentation and variable consideration against actual contracts rather than equating receipts with revenue. Invoice timing, revenue recognition, and cash collection need separate ledger fields. A thirty-six-month agreement provides a monitoring horizon, not permission to book thirty-six months of speculative savings on signature.

For b2b_class_action_contingency_recovery, build a TRACK_1 watchlist covering payment-card interchange, freight, auto parts, commercial insurance, and SaaS settlements. Some corporate antitrust funds reach multibillion-dollar scale, but fund size says nothing about one business's payable award. Treat the often-cited 85–90% nonfiling premise as a cohort hypothesis to validate against administrator reports, not a universal conversion statistic. Monitor official settlement sites, court orders, claim deadlines, class definitions, exclusions, and distribution updates. A parser may flag a client whose primary processor or vendor statements overlap the class period; a reviewer must verify the operating entity, eligible purchases, releases, and prior submissions. Use the required fallback of filing strictly for verified operating businesses with primary statements and court-approved third-party claim-filing riders. Where the court or administrator does not permit the arrangement, stop that filing route rather than relabeling the agency relationship. At a 25–33% contingent share, a verified $12,000 payout yields $3,000–$3,960, subject to permitted terms. Model neither face-value purchases nor advertised settlement funds as collectible revenue. Proration, objections, appeals, and distribution schedules can change both amount and timing. Keep claim acknowledgment, adjudication, payment, and operator collection distinct. The strongest outreach artifact is an eligibility checklist tied to primary records, not an inflated recovery estimate.

sections.heading: 4. Compound distribution while rehearsing failure recovery
paragraphs: Build distribution around a useful eligibility artifact rather than generic recovery promises. Publish programmatic pages only when each page contains a genuinely distinct utility jurisdiction, carrier rule, or settlement class with an authoritative source and review date. A Python job can refresh source fingerprints and open an editorial task when terms change; it should not automatically publish model-written interpretations. The conversion offer is a narrow diagnostic requiring only minimum account attributes, followed by secure evidence intake after authorization. For an illustrative cohort, 200 relevant visitors producing twenty diagnostic requests and five qualified engagements represent 10% request conversion and 25% request-to-engagement conversion. If content and distribution cost $600, acquisition cost is $120 per engagement before sales labor. Compare that figure with collected contribution over a defined cohort period, not a thirty-six-month theoretical contract total. Close the referral loop by asking a satisfied client to share a client-approved savings summary containing methodology and verified results but no account identifiers. Never publish tax-preparer information merely because the same client approved an unrelated parcel case study. The resulting artifact attracts similar operating profiles, which improves extraction templates and qualification rules. This is the flywheel: better evidence produces better segmentation, better segmentation produces cleaner records, and cleaner records reduce review cost.

Accountants, payroll providers, property managers, and logistics advisers offer better context than indiscriminate prospect lists. Create partner-specific intake links that attribute introductions without exposing another client's files or tax status. A partner receives a checklist, authority template, expected evidence request, and status vocabulary; they do not receive unrestricted access to the recovery ledger. For a monthly pilot, ten active partners producing two introductions each yield twenty introductions. At 30% qualification and a 50% close rate, that creates three engagements. A $450 enablement budget implies $150 acquisition expense per engagement before owner time and any permitted referral compensation. Check professional referral restrictions and disclose arrangements where required before offering compensation. Outbound messages should identify one plausible operational condition, such as multi-location utility billing, without claiming a refund has already been found. Apply 15 U.S.C. §7704 requirements for commercial email, including accurate headers, identification where required, a valid postal address, and timely opt-out handling. Synchronize suppression across campaigns and partners rather than merely hiding a contact from one list. A language model can draft from approved factual templates; a person approves new claims and targeting logic. Measure qualified engagements and retained clients, not message volume, because poor-fit traffic consumes the same scarce specialist review capacity as legitimate cases.

Make failure recovery an explicit service capability before adding volume. Webhooks require authenticated delivery, replay protection, bounded payloads, and durable acknowledgment only after the event is safely recorded. Use per-client queues and concurrency limits so one malformed utility export cannot block parcel deadlines across the book. Poison messages enter an exception queue with source fingerprint, error category, retry history, and named owner; they never disappear into a generic log. For deadline-sensitive WOTC work, schedule a daily ATS-versus-ledger reconciliation independent of webhook delivery. For carrier outages, preserve prepared claims and switch to the contractually accepted manual route before the filing window closes. For municipal delays, update client status and cash forecasts without repeatedly submitting the same request. Version prompts, extraction schemas, tariff rules, and fee calculations, then replay a fixed reviewed test set before deployment. Include contradictory invoices, duplicate shipments, meter rollovers, late hires, and settlement entities with similar names. A failed test blocks the changed component while unaffected lanes continue. The Scaled team adds a second full-time operator and a fourth contractor only when measured queue age, review utilization, and collected contribution justify the handoff. Maintain a weekly drill that reconstructs one case from original evidence through collected fee; scalability means another authorized operator can reproduce the result.

sop_steps.title: Authorize and snapshot
sop_steps.action: Obtain scoped authority and preserve original account evidence before account-specific findings leave the team.
sop_steps.detail: Record client identity, permitted channels, baseline periods, fee terms, disclosure restrictions, and source fingerprints in the tenant ledger.

sop_steps.title: Extract and test
sop_steps.action: Run deterministic normalization and constrained model extraction against versioned eligibility rules.
sop_steps.detail: Reject arithmetic mismatches, missing provenance, stale tariffs, duplicate claims, unsupported units, and incomplete deadline evidence into assigned exception queues.

sop_steps.title: Review and transmit
sop_steps.action: Have the qualified reviewer approve the exact payload before submission through an authorized channel.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve reviewer identity, approved payload fingerprint, submission identifier, acknowledgment, and the no-duplicate retry decision.

sop_steps.title: Reconcile and compound
sop_steps.action: Reconcile realized outcomes and earned fees, then update reviewed templates and permitted referral artifacts.
sop_steps.detail: Separate client recovery from operator revenue, measure automation and acquisition costs, and replay failures before expanding the affected workflow.

chapters.pull_quote: Automate the evidence trail, not the entitlement decision, and scale only the recoveries another reviewer can reproduce.
action_checklist: Create twelve lane records with explicit authority, evidence, fee basis, reviewer credentials, deadlines, and overlapping-recovery identifiers.
Implement tenant-scoped event intake with source fingerprints, idempotent submission records, bounded retries, and an assigned exception queue.
Connect only authorized FedEx/UPS interfaces, register effective utility tariffs, and reconcile ATS hires against timely Form 8850 evidence.
Benchmark a frozen task inventory against the 70%+ automation target while separately measuring review minutes and cost per completed run.
Reconcile the three canonical revenue and owner-profit cases without counting client refunds, credits, settlement principal, or future savings as current operator revenue.
Launch one reviewed research-page cohort and one partner cohort, then rehearse carrier, municipal, and ATS failure recovery before increasing intake.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 1 FT + 3 C (4 people) -> 2 FT + 4 C (6 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?
chapters.title: Pod Architecture, Contractor KPIs & Exit Valuation
chapters.subtitle: Four-to-Six-Person Recovery Pods, FedEx/UPS Claim Controls, WOTC Evidence, ASC 606 Cohorts & Written IP Transfers
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #38, Contingent Corporate Bill-Audit & Tax-Credit Recovery, ranks #06 of 42 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 12 mapped plays become transferable assets only when authorization, evidence, specialist judgment, collection, and ownership survive the founder's absence. Start with one full-time operator and three specialist contractors; add an operations lead and evidence contractor only against demonstrated capacity pressure. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled. This chapter converts those cases into seat charters, compensation controls, weekly denominators, customer and counterparty exposure limits, and cohort accounting. It also separates earned operator fees from client recoveries and explains why documented transferability, rather than speculative refund inventory, supports a stronger exit or a durable cash-producing book.

sections.heading: 1. Assign twelve plays to four accountable seats before adding people
paragraphs: Candidate #38 needs a shared production system, not twelve separate departments. For staffing, map its twelve plays into four delivery lanes: P01 FedEx service refunds, P02 UPS service refunds, P03 parcel duplicate and accessorial corrections, P04 electric tariff recovery, P05 gas tariff recovery, P06 water and sewer adjustments including cooling-tower deductions, P07 waste and telecom billing corrections, P08 property assessment appeals, P09 property exemption and classification corrections, P10 WOTC screening and certification, P11 WOTC substantiation and processing, and P12 specialty tax-credit recovery through appropriately qualified practitioners. These are operating workstreams within the supplied opportunity, not twelve independent revenue forecasts. One full-time owner controls sales, engagement economics, cash reconciliation, and client communication. Contractor A owns parcel evidence and carrier submissions; Contractor B owns utility, waste, telecom, and property evidence; Contractor C owns tax-credit documentation and permitted practitioner work. Every case has exactly one delivery owner and one named reviewer. The owner reviews commercial arithmetic and authority, while technical opinions stay with a qualified specialist. If Contractor B lacks a required property-tax license, that play remains inactive until the seat is filled appropriately. Do not hide extra subcontractors inside the four-person staffing claim.

Write each contractor charter around accepted deliverables rather than nominal availability. A parcel packet includes the invoice, tracking event history, applicable service commitment, waiver assessment, filing deadline, submission identifier, and expected operator fee. A utility packet includes the account authorization, historical tariff, meter identifiers, baseline invoices, calculation workbook, and adjustment request. A property packet adds assessment notices, jurisdictional deadlines, representation authority, and licensed review where required. A tax packet adds eligibility evidence, certification status, preparer responsibility, and the engagement-specific fee analysis. Set contractual targets of two business days for intake triage, three for a complete routine evidence packet, and one for correcting a material QA defect. These are internal service commitments, not promises about utility refund issuance or state certification timing. Measure specialists against work they can control. Test contractor status under the applicable federal and state standards; a contract label does not resolve a relationship that actually operates as employment. Require individual access, confidentiality, written IP assignment, and explicit limits on delegation. Contractors choose their methods within agreed evidence and security requirements; the owner purchases accountable outputs rather than quietly managing three additional employees.

Move to two full-time employees and four contractors only when eight consecutive weekly scorecards show a profitable queue that the existing pod cannot clear without missed deadlines or weakened review. The second employee becomes operations lead, taking intake, capacity planning, exception routing, and ledger reconciliation away from the founder. The fourth contractor becomes evidence and integration specialist, maintaining carrier exports, OCR exception queues, ATS field mappings, and document manifests across all twelve plays. That seat does not make tax judgments or sign property appeals without the required authority. Keep the founder responsible for acquisition, pricing, concentration management, and quarterly client retention. Use a capacity sheet with accepted packets per week, median review minutes, deadline exposure, and earned fee contribution after direct contractor cost. A backlog of speculative credits is not a hiring signal. A backlog of authorized, documented, economically positive cases can be. Model the full loaded employee cost before issuing an offer, and fund the transition from collected operator fees rather than anticipated client refunds. At six people, every recurring process should have a trained backup, but technical backups must possess the same required credentials as the primary seat.

callout.title: Build specialist leverage without buying invisible headcount
callout.body: The highest-value contractor deliverable is a reproducible case that another authorized specialist can finish without discovery work.
items: Have Contractor A inspect the customer's negotiated FedEx or UPS waiver terms before importing a year's shipments into a refund queue.
Have Contractor B photograph cooling-tower meter serials and reconcile them to the deduction account before calculating sewer savings.
Have Contractor C preserve the Form 8850 submission timestamp and state workforce agency receipt separately from the ATS screening result.
Have the integration contractor package mappings, job configuration, exception handling, and restoration instructions before accepting any automation milestone.

sections.heading: 2. Pay for accepted evidence and run one denominator-driven weekly scorecard
paragraphs: Compensation should reward usable evidence and realized economics, not the number of claims submitted. For parcel and utility contractors, an illustrative commercial arrangement is a fixed fee for an accepted packet plus a collection bonus calculated on the operator's earned, collected fee, never on the client's entire refund. If a client receives a $10,000 utility refund and the engagement earns a 30% share, operator revenue is $3,000. A $150 packet fee and 10% collection bonus produce $450 of direct contractor cost and $2,550 before other delivery and overhead costs. These illustrative unit terms do not replace the canonical scenario margins. Define acceptance, rework, payment timing, duplicate claims, reversals, and disputed collections in writing. Do not impose the same contingent structure on federal tax-return work: Treasury Circular 230 section 10.27, applicable judicial limits, professional rules, and the actual service determine permissible terms. Fixed document-processing or hourly specialist compensation may be appropriate, but relabeling a prohibited contingent arrangement does not cure it. Require engagement-specific review before quoting tax fees. Pay accepted contractor invoices promptly under their contract even when the operator chose a client collection cycle that creates working-capital pressure.

Run a forty-five-minute weekly meeting from a frozen Monday snapshot, using the same definitions for all twelve plays. Intake completeness equals authorized cases containing every required baseline document divided by cases received. First-pass acceptance equals packets accepted without material correction divided by packets reviewed. Submission timeliness equals eligible, authorized cases submitted before their documented deadline divided by all such cases reaching a deadline that week; missed cases remain in the denominator. Recovery realization compares confirmed recoveries with submitted amounts for sufficiently mature cohorts, separating denials from counterparty delay. Collection conversion compares collected operator fees with invoices due for the selected cohort, not with this week's speculative pipeline. Start with internal targets of 95% intake completeness, 98% first-pass acceptance, and 100% deadline compliance, then revise capacity rather than quietly weakening definitions. Display median and ninetieth percentile case age so a few municipal refunds cannot disappear inside an average. Every red metric gets an owner, corrective action, and due date. Carry unresolved items forward. A specialist's excellent win rate is meaningless if they quietly exclude hard cases or withhold rejected packets from the queue.

QA starts with complete review of every new contractor's first twenty packets and every newly activated play. After a documented clean run, review all high-value, tax, property, deadline-sensitive, and unusual-tariff cases, plus a random 10% of routine low-risk packets. Any material error returns the affected workflow to complete review until twenty consecutive packets pass. Material means wrong authority, wrong account, unsupported eligibility, incorrect fee basis, duplicate submission, or a missed statutory or contractual deadline; spelling corrections do not inflate the defect rate. Keep sampling reproducible with a saved case list and selection seed. Score contractor performance separately from carrier, utility, municipal, or state-agency response time. Track external waiting days, internal idle days, and client document delays as distinct clocks. Use carrier-authorized APIs or EDI access under the applicable terms, with retry limits, submission deduplication, and receipt reconciliation. For WOTC, verify that the employee's start date falls within an effective statutory authorization period, and track the generally applicable 28-day certification-request deadline under 26 U.S.C. section 51(d)(13). Screening software does not establish credit eligibility, extend a deadline, or substitute for agency certification.

sop_steps.title: Freeze the operating snapshot
sop_steps.action: Export the case register, receivables, contractor invoices, and deadline queue every Monday.
sop_steps.detail: Record snapshot time, cohort definitions, omitted-source exceptions, and responsible seat before calculating any percentage.

sop_steps.action: Match submission receipts, confirmed recoveries, fee invoices, and cash deposits by case identifier.
sop_steps.detail: Separate missing evidence, internal delay, counterparty delay, disputed fees, and reversals so each exception has an actionable cause.

sop_steps.action: Give every missed target a named owner, deadline, and measurable repair.

sop_steps.action: Verify the prior week's corrective work before authorizing new capacity commitments.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve the frozen scorecard and resolution evidence so a buyer can reconstruct management decisions without relying on founder recollection.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile earned fees, aging cohorts, and concentration before calling it profit
paragraphs: The canonical scorecard contains three annual operator-revenue cases, not three measures of client spending. Conservative revenue is $110,000, costs are $77,000, and owner net profit is $33,000 at 30%. Base revenue is $505,000, costs are $287,850, and owner net profit is $217,150 at 43.0%. Scaled revenue is $900,000, costs are $396,000, and owner net profit is $504,000 at 56%. The first two cases use one full-time employee and three contractors; the third uses two full-time employees and four contractors. Earned contingency refund shares, earned shared-savings fees, and WOTC processing fees compose revenue. Underlying utility bills, freight spend, property values, and client tax credits do not. For a $100,000 confirmed client recovery with an enforceable 30% operator share, the fee basis is $30,000, not $100,000. Apply ASC 606 to the actual performance obligation, variable consideration constraint, and principal-versus-agent facts. Do not subtract the client's 70% share from revenue a second time after already reporting the operator's retained fee. Direct contractor expense is a separate cost unless the specific contractual arrangement supports different presentation. Keep these classifications consistent across forecasts, monthly closes, contractor scorecards, and buyer diligence.

Build an accrual subledger with client, play, authorization date, service period, submission cohort, counterparty, expected recovery, confirmed recovery, earned operator fee, invoice date, cash receipt, contractor cost, and reversal history. Expected recoveries belong in the operating pipeline until recognition requirements are met; a spreadsheet probability is not sufficient evidence of earned revenue. For a 36-month shared-savings engagement, preserve the signed baseline, adjustment method, verification frequency, termination terms, and each period's calculation. If verified monthly savings are $4,000 and the share is 25%, the operator's monthly fee is $1,000. Multiplying that by 36 produces a potential contract stream, not automatic day-one revenue. Assess recognition over the actual service and entitlement pattern, including any variable consideration constraint. Reconcile the subledger monthly to bank deposits, accounts receivable, credits, and contractor liabilities. Separately disclose receivable aging and expected credit losses rather than silently reducing the measured win rate. Client recovery funds should ordinarily flow directly to the client; any collection-agent arrangement needs explicit authority, appropriate account controls, and a liability ledger. That prevents client money from masquerading as available payroll cash or operator earnings.

Set two hard portfolio caps at no more than 25%: one customer group may contribute at most 25% of trailing twelve-month recognized operator revenue, and one recovery counterparty group may account for at most 25% of both open expected operator-fee exposure and trailing recognized operator revenue. Aggregate related customer entities and counterparty affiliates; splitting account numbers does not diversify economic dependence. For shared-savings fees, classify the underlying utility or provider that sustains the savings stream, not merely the customer paying the invoice. Classify tax exposure by the relevant administering authority and program dependency, with a separate correlated-program stress view. A startup with one client necessarily breaches the customer cap, so disclose that concentration and prohibit claims of a diversified transferable book until it is cured. At 20%, route incremental sales toward other customers, counterparties, and plays. At 25%, pause additional exposure to that group while fulfilling existing obligations. Review a 90-day refund-delay stress case and the loss of the largest customer against cash reserves and committed contractor payments. Federal credit exposure and municipal delays require different timing assumptions even when their historical collection percentages look similar.

callout.title: Verify four conditions before releasing a case into production
callout.body: A complete intake record protects fee entitlement, filing accuracy, and the future transferability of the book.
items: Verify signed engagement, Letter of Authorization, access scope, and baseline invoice snapshots before disclosing tariff findings or submitting a refund request.
Verify carrier waiver status, filing windows, applicable tariff periods, property representation credentials, and the correct recovery recipient.
Verify tax-credit statutory availability for the relevant dates, Form 8850 timing where applicable, supporting evidence, practitioner scope, and permissible fee terms.
Verify customer and counterparty exposure, recognition treatment, contractor acceptance criteria, and a qualified reviewer before adding the case to capacity commitments.

sections.heading: 4. Transfer evidence, rights, and management before negotiating an exit multiple
paragraphs: A transferable book consists of enforceable engagements, reproducible evidence, owned operating assets, and relationships that survive the founder's departure. Obtain written assignments of contractor-created copyright interests under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), signed by the rights owner, rather than assuming every independent contractor deliverable is work made for hire. Identify pre-existing tools separately and secure licenses broad enough for continued operation and the contemplated transaction. Include calculation templates, OCR mappings, submission scripts, training materials, and documentation; the assignment does not transfer client records the operator never owned. Inventory customer confidentiality obligations, data-processing restrictions, carrier API terms, software licenses, and engagement assignment or change-of-control clauses. A buyer cannot inherit personal practitioner credentials or assume a Letter of Authorization automatically covers a different entity. Build a restricted diligence room with redacted samples first, then release identifiable records only under appropriate contractual authority and access controls. Demonstrate that a new authorized operator can reconstruct a claim from source documents, calculate the fee, identify the deadline, and reconcile collection without asking the founder where the evidence lives. That exercise exposes missing rights and undocumented judgment before they become purchase-price deductions.

Use valuation multiples as explicit negotiating assumptions, not as verified market quotations. For planning, test a small owner-operated book at 2.0 to 3.0 times normalized seller's discretionary earnings, and a genuinely manager-run, diversified book at 3.0 to 4.5 times normalized EBITDA. These illustrative ranges require transaction evidence before being presented as market support. Neither metric automatically equals canonical owner net profit. Reconcile owner compensation, replacement labor, interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, recurring technology costs, and defensible one-time adjustments. As a sensitivity only, if the $217,150 Base owner-profit figure needed just a $100,000 annual replacement-manager deduction and no other adjustments, the resulting earnings proxy would be $117,150; applying 3.0 to 4.5 times gives $351,450 to $527,175. That illustration does not reclassify the canonical profit figure or prove EBITDA. Distinguish enterprise value from seller proceeds after debt, cash treatment, working-capital adjustment, transaction costs, and taxes. Expect contingent consideration where revenue depends on disputed credits, aging refunds, or customer consent to assignment. Define earnout revenue using the same recognition policies and specify who controls collections, staffing, dispute settlements, and allocation of shared costs.

Premium pricing is earned by reducing the buyer's uncertainty, not by describing a contingent pipeline as recurring revenue. Supply at least twenty-four months of cohort reporting where available, distinguish repeat customers from contracted recurring fees, and disclose shorter operating history plainly. Show retention by customer group, remaining enforceable shared-savings periods, cancellation rights, realized fee yields, reversals, contractor turnover, and concentration trends. Conduct a thirty-day founder-absence rehearsal: the operations lead runs scorecards, contractors deliver accepted packets, client updates ship on schedule, and the founder intervenes only for documented reserved decisions. Log every intervention and repair the underlying dependency. If sale economics disappoint, the same controls support a durable cash cow. Distribute cash only after funding committed delivery costs, ordinary overhead, expected credits or reversals, and a documented delay reserve; a profitable accrual statement does not settle overdue contractor invoices. Review acquisition channels quarterly so one referral partner cannot quietly become the real source of dependence behind diversified customers. Keep all twelve plays available only where the pod has current competence and authority. A smaller verified book with reliable handoffs is more transferable than a larger collection of unsupported claims and founder promises.

chapters.pull_quote: A premium book is not a pile of claims; it is earned fees, owned methods, and qualified people who can deliver without the founder.
action_checklist: Assign P01 through P12 to the founder and three named contractors, documenting credentials, permitted work, deliverable ownership, and qualified backup coverage.
Execute contractor agreements covering accepted-packet compensation, rework SLAs, confidentiality, access restrictions, and signed copyright assignments under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a).
Launch the Monday scorecard with fixed denominators for completeness, first-pass acceptance, deadline performance, mature-cohort realization, collections, and internal idle time.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #38 ranks #06 of 42 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, but launch success depends on recoverable evidence, not impressive client bill totals. This sprint translates 12 mapped plays into a controlled operating queue for one full-time owner and three contractors. Days 1–7 establish authority, evidence standards, and a $6,000 launch ceiling; Days 8–14 secure usable account records; Days 15–21 submit defensible claims; Days 22–30 reconcile acknowledgments and choose Kill, Fix, or Scale. Day 60 and Day 90 thresholds distinguish weak acquisition from slow utility payments. The canonical annual owner-profit cases remain $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled. The sprint validates their operating prerequisites without treating disputed refunds, client tax credits, or projected savings as earned operator revenue.
