sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Establish Authority, Twelve Play Codes, and a Bounded Pod
paragraphs: Day 1 begins with a narrower commitment than the shelf title suggests: operate two evidence-ready lanes, not twelve simultaneous services. For this sprint, map the twelve plays into explicit queue codes: P01 UPS service-guarantee refunds; P02 FedEx service-guarantee refunds; P03 duplicate parcel charges; P04 parcel weight and dimension corrections; P05 commercial utility rate-class corrections; P06 utility meter and demand-billing errors; P07 cooling-tower sewer deductions; P08 waste-service billing discrepancies; P09 telecom inventory and billing corrections; P10 property-assessment appeals; P11 WOTC processing; and P12 specialty-credit screening with qualified practitioners. This is the chapter's operating taxonomy, not a claim that every account qualifies for every play. Start with one parcel lane and one utility lane where records, contract rights, and competent reviewers already exist. Route P10 through jurisdiction-specific licensing and appeal deadlines; keep P11 and P12 inactive until hire-date authorization, practitioner scope, and fee treatment are established. Assign each prospect a primary code and optional secondary code, preventing the same recovery from entering two pipelines. A 12-play catalog creates cross-selling discipline only when every proposed expansion carries its own evidence checklist, owner, filing clock, and expected collection interval. Measure demand for dormant plays without promising delivery or collecting unnecessary employee records.

Build the four-person pod around one owner working forty hours weekly and three contractors budgeted at eight hours each. Those sixty-four hours are an illustrative capacity budget, not an implication that contractors supply full-time availability. Reserve sixteen hours for sales, administration, security, and rework, leaving forty-eight hours for onboarding, analysis, review, and claim follow-up. The owner controls pricing, client authority, collections, and exceptions. Contractor one handles parcel evidence and carrier submissions; contractor two handles utility tariffs, meter schedules, and billing reconstruction; contractor three handles independent review, bookkeeping support, and coordination with qualified specialists. Do not assign tax representation or licensed property work merely because a contractor can read invoices. Use Google Workspace with restricted client folders, a HubSpot pipeline containing minimal account metadata, and a spreadsheet ledger with unique case identifiers. Keep originals read-only, record document hashes where practical, and separate client authorization from carrier credentials. A signed Letter of Authorization must identify accounts, permitted actions, recipients, duration, and revocation procedure. Obtain baseline invoice snapshots before disclosing account-specific findings. Access to a billing portal does not itself establish authority to submit an appeal, change a rate class, or file a tax document. Each of those actions needs its own documented scope.

Set the first thirty-day cash ceiling at $6,000: $3,500 for setup and $2,500 for recurring launch operations. The setup envelope includes engagement drafting, secure onboarding configuration, contractor calibration, and an initial reserve; the operating envelope includes scheduled contractor time, software, outreach, and retrieval costs. Treat these as management allocations inside the stated $6,000–$35,000 startup range, not vendor quotations. Every purchase must fit a named envelope before commitment. The canonical monthly operating range of $1,500–$9,500 does not include permission to spend the upper bound during an unproven pilot. Reserve any Day 31–60 extension separately, rather than embedding automatic renewals in contractor agreements. Set a default expense-recovery fee example of thirty percent of verified client recovery, within the stated twenty-five-to-fifty-percent contingency range, with precise treatment of offsets, reversals, and disputed credits. Do not carry that fee structure automatically into federal tax work. Treasury Circular 230 section 10.27 restricts contingent fees for covered services, subject to its exceptions and applicable judicial limits. Use separately scoped fixed processing fees for initial WOTC work unless a qualified practitioner establishes another permitted structure. Day 7 ends with a priced, authorized, reviewable service—not a claim that zero-upfront client pricing removes operator cash risk.

callout.title: Four Pre-Flight Checks Before Any Client-Specific Submission
callout.body: A failure blocks the affected account or play until corrected; unrelated authorized work can continue.
items: Verify signed account-level authority, matching legal entity names, permitted recipients, and an unexpired authorization period.
Preserve original invoices, governing contract terms, current tariff versions, and a reproducible baseline before presenting findings.
Verify carrier waiver treatment, applicable claim deadlines, property-work licensing, and the responsible reviewer's actual credentials.
Confirm permitted fee treatment for each service, including Circular 230 scope and the WOTC hire-date authorization condition.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Convert Target Accounts into Complete, Testable Evidence
paragraphs: Days 8–14 turn prospecting into a measured acquisition experiment. Build a list of one hundred named employers or commercial accounts with plausible parcel volume or complex utility billing, using public business information and existing relationships rather than employee-level tax records. Choose a coherent segment, such as regional distributors with multiple shipping accounts, so one discovery script produces comparable evidence. The owner targets twenty completed discovery conversations by Day 30; the first week of outreach should schedule at least ten. A completed conversation records the billing decision-maker, account count, incumbent auditor, available history, contract restrictions, and willingness to sign an authorization. A message sent or an unanswered call is not a completed conversation. Ask directly whether the carrier agreement waives service-guarantee refunds and whether another provider already owns overlapping claims. Offer a narrow records review rather than an invented recovery estimate. Track refusals by reason: unavailable records, existing exclusivity, insufficient bill complexity, unacceptable fee terms, or lack of authority. These categories tell the owner whether to repair targeting, engagement language, or the service itself. The sprint seeks six signed authorizations and four complete datasets by Day 30; it does not assume six clients will produce collectible fees within the first month.

Define completeness before accepting the first file. For parcel work, request account identifiers, invoice detail, tracking events available through authorized channels, service codes, negotiated terms, adjustment history, and filing deadlines. FedEx and UPS developer interfaces do not establish a universal right to automate refunds; use only documented endpoints, approved integrations, or authorized portal procedures supporting the actual account. For utility work, obtain at least twelve consecutive billing periods when available, meter identifiers, service classification, rate schedules, taxes, demand readings, and prior adjustments. Shorter histories require a specific reason and a narrower claim scope. Cooling-tower deductions need the municipality's actual deduction rules and acceptable meter evidence, not an assumed percentage of water consumption. OCR output from Tesseract can accelerate extraction, but a reviewer must reconcile account number, dates, units, multiplier, and total against the source invoice. Use Decimal arithmetic in any Python calculation so rounding follows the tariff or contract. Declare a dataset complete only when the reviewer can reproduce the proposed comparison and establish its filing window. A large folder containing invoices but missing the governing agreement remains incomplete. Record the missing field and responsible client contact instead of allowing an analyst to silently substitute an industry average.

Treat tax-credit onboarding as a different evidence lane with different timing and access requirements. For WOTC, IRC section 51(d)(13) generally requires the pre-screening notice by the employment-offer date and submission to the designated local agency no later than twenty-eight days after work begins. Use the current Form 8850 instructions and state workforce agency procedure to implement that clock. The statutory termination rule in section 51(c)(4) must also be checked against the employee's start date; the authorization through December 31, 2025 does not establish eligibility for later starts without a subsequent statutory extension. Record the effective authority instead of treating continued form availability as proof of eligibility. An ATS integration should transmit only necessary fields through restricted access, maintain submission acknowledgments, and preserve certification and qualified-wage support. Hours worked, targeted-group certification, wages, and employer tax circumstances determine the credit; a new hire alone does not. Where tax-return information is involved, evaluate 26 U.S.C. sections 7216 and 6713 and their implementing exceptions before contractor disclosure. Keep P11 inactive if these prerequisites are unresolved. The owner can still sell and deliver authorized parcel and utility work, preserving the sprint's momentum without turning a statutory timing defect into a speculative credit receivable.

callout.title: Four Tactics That Preserve Small-Team Recovery Economics
callout.body: Experienced operators remove entitlement and evidence ambiguity before spending scarce analyst hours.
items: Ask for the carrier agreement before downloading thousands of shipment rows; a service-guarantee waiver can eliminate the headline recovery thesis.
Read utility effective dates before comparing rates; a legitimate seasonal or annual tariff change can resemble a recoverable overcharge.
Capture adjustment identifiers before submitting parcel claims; prior credits otherwise create duplicate requests and overstated recovery totals.
Separate sewer-deduction meter evidence from general water invoices; local acceptance rules often control whether the deduction survives review.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Submit Defensible Claims and Establish the Fee Ledger
paragraphs: Days 15–21 should produce a small number of defensible cases rather than a large speculative recovery total. A case becomes evidence-cleared only after authorization, eligibility, arithmetic, duplicate screening, filing timing, and independent review all pass. It becomes submitted only when the receiving carrier, utility, agency, or authorized channel provides a submission record. It becomes accepted when that recipient acknowledges the substantive adjustment or entitlement, not merely receipt of an email. Maintain these states separately from earned fee, invoiced fee, and collected cash. For a parcel example, a verified $10,000 client credit at a thirty-percent fee creates a potential $3,000 operator fee, subject to the engagement's earning condition and reversals. It does not create $10,000 of operator revenue. A shared-savings engagement running thirty-six months needs a locked baseline, agreed normalization rules, monthly verification, and an explicit billing schedule. Do not book all thirty-six projected installments on signature. Track the future schedule as a contract forecast and recognize earned amounts under the actual performance obligations and applicable accounting treatment. Where another specialist controls the service and the pod acts as agent, evaluate ASC 606 principal-versus-agent presentation and retain only the appropriate net operator share in revenue.

Assign the first submission batch to the two active lanes and cap work in progress at four analytical accounts. With forty-eight delivery hours weekly, a planning allowance of six hours for each complete account leaves twenty-four hours for review, filings, follow-up, and difficult exceptions. Record actual time by play code before assuming this allowance is achievable. Parcel cases should preserve shipment-level identifiers, the applicable service commitment, claim basis, adjustment checks, and the exact response. Utility cases should preserve billed units, correct tariff treatment, the resulting difference, and the authority for the requested adjustment. Cooling-tower cases additionally need accepted meter installation and deduction evidence where local rules require them. Contractor three independently recalculates every first-batch claim; sampling is premature while error patterns remain unmeasured. A missed deadline, unsupported authority, or double-counted credit is a material defect even if the arithmetic is correct. Correct defects before submission and record rework hours against the account's economics. Do not bypass a portal restriction with undocumented automation. When an API lacks a supported claim operation, use the permitted manual procedure and measure its labor burden. An attractive automation narrative is irrelevant if the carrier's account terms remove the recovery right or prohibit the proposed access method.

Reconcile the launch ledger to Formula v2.0 without converting pilot targets into annual promises. The Conservative case is $110,000 operator revenue less $77,000 total costs, leaving $33,000 at thirty percent. The Base case is $505,000 less $287,850, leaving $217,150 at 43.0 percent. The Scaled case is $900,000 less $396,000, leaving $504,000 at fifty-six percent. Conservative and Base both use one full-time owner plus three contractors; Scaled requires two full-time people plus four contractors. Those totals include the scorecard's aggregate cost burden, not merely the software subscriptions visible during launch. The monthly operating range must therefore remain separate from annual all-in costs that include variable delivery expense. For case decisions, calculate contribution as earned operator fees minus attributable contractor work, retrieval costs, and expected fee reversals. Divide by earned operator fees only when that denominator is positive. This case contribution is not the annual owner-profit margin, because acquisition and general overhead still need funding. Likewise, a thirty-percent contingency rate is a pricing percentage, not a thirty-percent profit margin. Maintain separate columns for client recovery, retained operator fee, direct cost, overhead allocation, and cash receipt so the owner cannot mistake large client bill totals for a profitable operating business.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30 and Beyond: Apply Quantitative Kill, Fix, or Scale Decisions
paragraphs: Days 22–30 close the experiment by resolving exceptions and testing measurable prerequisites. These thresholds are proposed management rules, not additional scorecard scenarios. At Day 30, Scale requires six signed account authorizations, four complete datasets, two evidence-cleared cases, and at least $10,000 of supported potential operator fees across distinct cases. Value that pipeline using verified client recovery and contracted retained shares, excluding unvalidated leads and overlapping claims. Require zero unresolved material defects and paid-plus-committed launch spending no higher than $6,000. Scale at this checkpoint means expanding acquisition inside the existing pod, not hiring the Scaled scenario's six-person team. Kill the tested acquisition approach if one hundred named accounts and twenty completed discovery conversations yield fewer than two signed authorizations. Do not apply that conversion verdict when the owner failed to complete the test. Otherwise choose Fix, identify the largest bottleneck, assign one owner, and run a fourteen-day corrective experiment without increasing active lanes. Stop new discretionary spending whenever the ceiling is exceeded. Zero collected fees at Day 30 alone does not trigger Kill: the candidate's stated time to first deal is one to four months, and utility issuance can take longer than the initial sprint.

At Day 60, Scale requires ten authorizations, eight complete datasets, six submitted cases, three substantively accepted cases, $7,500 in earned operator fees, $3,000 collected, and $25,000 in evidence-cleared potential fees. Require at least fifty-percent case contribution on earned fees and no unresolved material defects. The cumulative cash ceiling is $9,000, available only after a separately authorized $3,000 extension. Kill the tested lane if eight complete analytical accounts produce fewer than three evidence-cleared cases; this measures weak entitlement density rather than recipient payment speed. All other shortfalls produce Fix unless a hard-stop issue requires immediate suspension. At Day 90, Scale requires fifteen authorizations, twelve complete datasets, ten submissions, six substantive acceptances, $20,000 earned fees, $12,000 collected, and $40,000 in evidence-cleared potential fees. Keep case contribution at or above fifty percent and cumulative spending within $12,000 after another separately authorized extension. Kill a lane with contribution below thirty percent across at least six accepted, fee-earned cases, or zero acceptances from ten matured submissions. Matured means the documented recipient response interval and one scheduled follow-up interval have elapsed; log extensions supported by the recipient. A slow municipal payment does not become a failed claim simply because the operator wants quicker cash.

Apply hard stops before commercial thresholds: compromised access, absent authority, prohibited fee treatment, or an unsupported filing requires immediate suspension of the affected activity. Then apply the stated Kill tests; only businesses passing every Scale condition advance, while the remainder enter Fix. Track results by lane and cohort so profitable parcel work does not hide an uneconomic utility workflow. Use no more than two Fix cycles of fourteen days without a fresh written budget decision and evidence of a specific improving metric. A fix must name its measurable target, such as raising complete-dataset conversion from two of six authorizations to four of six, or reducing median review time from four hours to two. Scaling also requires delivery headroom: keep committed delivery work below eighty percent of the forty-eight-hour weekly allowance before adding accounts. That leaves fewer than 38.4 scheduled hours committed to current cases and protects urgent filing work. If demand exceeds this limit, change intake timing before promising more service. The six-person Scaled pod is a later capacity decision supported by repeatable collections and funded staffing, not a Day 90 entitlement. Close the sprint with a signed decision memo identifying the surviving plays, the next cash ceiling, the accountable owner, and the exact date of the next evidence-based review.
